akhfash:9-11.t: He said ﴿يَوْمَ تَمُورُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ مَوْراً﴾ ﴿وَتَسِيرُ ٱلْجِبَالُ سَيْراً﴾ ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾: the fāʾ came in because it has the meaning of "when such-and-such happens", so it resembles the conditional, because the conditional has its khabar (apodosis) with fāʾ.

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ ٱلْمَنُونِ﴾ because you say: "تَرَبَّصْتُ زَيْداً" (I waited for Zayd), i.e. I waited for him (تربصت به).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالطُّورِ﴾ that is, the mountain on which Allah spoke to Moses.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَكِتَابٍ مَسْطُورٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here; the gloss follows in the next entry.]

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿فِي رَقٍّ مَنْشُورٍ﴾ that is, the Torah or the Quran.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَالْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ﴾ It is in the third, or the sixth, or the seventh heaven, opposite the Kaaba; seventy thousand angels visit it every day for circumambulation and prayer, never returning to it again.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَالْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ﴾ that is, the filled one.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ لَوَاقِعٌ﴾ will surely come down upon the one who deserves it;

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ governed (maʿmūl) by لَوَاقِعٌ; ﴿تَمُورُ السَّمَاءُ مَوْرًا﴾ it moves and revolves,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَتَسِيرُ الْجِبَالُ سَيْرًا﴾ they become scattered dust; and that is on the Day of Resurrection.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ severity of punishment ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ of the messengers,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي خَوْضٍ﴾ of falsehood ﴿يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ that is, they occupy themselves with their disbelief.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا﴾ they are pushed violently; a badal (substitute) for يَوْمَ تَمُورُ. And it is said to them, by way of reproach:

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿هَذِهِ النَّارُ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾. [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿أَفَسِحْرٌ هَذَا﴾ — the punishment which you see — just as you used to say of the revelation "This is sorcery"? ﴿أَمْ أَنْتُمْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿اصْلَوْهَا فَاصْبِرُوا﴾ upon it ﴿أَوْ لَا تَصْبِرُوا﴾ your patience and your anguish are ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ because your patience will not benefit you; ﴿إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ that is, the recompense of it.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿فَاكِهِينَ﴾ delighting ﴿بِمَا﴾ maṣdariyya (the مَا that forms a maṣdar) ﴿آتَاهُمْ﴾ He has given them, ﴿رَبُّهُمْ وَوَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ conjoined to آتَاهُمْ, that is: in His giving them and His protecting them. And it is said to them:

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, enjoying it wholesomely; ﴿بِمَا﴾ the bāʾ is causal; ﴿كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustakinn) pronoun in His words, Exalted is He, فِي جَنَّاتٍ; ﴿عَلَى سُرُرٍ مَصْفُوفَةٍ﴾ one beside the other; ﴿وَزَوَّجْنَاهُمْ﴾ conjoined to فِي جَنَّاتٍ, that is, We paired them ﴿بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾ large-eyed, beautiful ones.

celaleyn:21-21.t:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to آمَنُوا [وَأَتْبَعْنَاهُمْ] ﴿ذُرِّيَّاتُهُمْ﴾ the young and the old [ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ] ﴿بِإِيمَانٍ﴾ on the part of the older ones, and on the part of the fathers in the case of the young ones; and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ﴾ those mentioned, in Paradise, so that they are in their rank even if they did not do as they did, as an honour to the fathers by gathering the children to them [ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ]; ﴿وَمَا أَلَتْنَاهُمْ﴾ with fatḥa and kasra on the lām: We did not diminish them ﴿مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ to be added to the work of the children; ﴿كُلُّ امْرِئٍ بِمَا كَسَبَ﴾ of work, good or evil, ﴿رَهِينٌ﴾ pledged: he is held to account for evil and rewarded for good.
[Translator's note: the bracketed Arabic words are variant readings given in the source text.]

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَأَمْدَدْنَاهُمْ﴾ We increase them time after time ﴿بِفَاكِهَةٍ وَلَحْمٍ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ even if they do not explicitly ask for it.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿يَتَنَازَعُونَ﴾ they pass among themselves ﴿فِيهَا﴾ that is, in Paradise, ﴿كَأْسًا﴾ wine; ﴿لَا لَغْوٌ فِيهَا﴾ that is, occurring among them because of drinking it, ﴿وَلَا تَأْثِيمٌ﴾ attaching to them through it, unlike the wine of this world.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ in service ﴿غِلْمَانٌ﴾ servants ﴿لَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ in beauty and delicacy ﴿لُؤْلُؤٌ مَكْنُونٌ﴾ guarded in the shell, because in it it is more beautiful than elsewhere.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ﴾ they ask one another about what they used to be in and what they have attained, out of delight and in acknowledgement of the blessing.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ hinting at the cause of their attainment: ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ فِي أَهْلِنَا﴾ in this world ﴿مُشْفِقِينَ﴾ fearful of Allah's punishment;

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا﴾ with forgiveness ﴿وَوَقَانَا عَذَابَ السَّمُومِ﴾ that is, the Fire, [so called] because it enters the pores. And they said, also as a hint:

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ that is, in this world, ﴿نَدْعُوهُ﴾ that is, we worshipped Him, affirming His oneness; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ with kasra, as a resumptive clause, even though it gives a reason in meaning; and with fatḥa, giving a reason in wording; ﴿هُوَ الْبَرُّ﴾ the Beneficent, true to His promise, ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ great in mercy.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾ continue reminding the idolaters and do not turn back from it because of their saying to you "a soothsayer, a madman"; ﴿فَمَا أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَتِ رَبِّكَ﴾ that is, by His favour upon you, ﴿بِكَاهِنٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of مَا ﴿وَلَا مَجْنُونٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ (meaning: rather) ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ he is ﴿شَاعِرٌ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ﴾ the vicissitudes of time, so that he perishes like other poets.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا﴾ my destruction, ﴿فَإِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ﴾ your destruction; and they were punished by the sword on the day of Badr. التَّرَبُّصُ means waiting.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلَامُهُمْ﴾ their minds ﴿بِهَذَا﴾ that is, their saying of him "a sorcerer, a soothsayer, a poet, a madman"? That is, they do not command them to do so. ﴿أَمْ﴾ (meaning: rather) ﴿هُمْ قَوْمٌ طَاغُونَ﴾ in their obstinacy.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُ﴾ he invented the Quran? He did not invent it; ﴿بَلْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ out of arrogance. If they say he invented it,

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿فَلْيَأْتُوا بِحَدِيثٍ﴾ invented ﴿مِثْلِهِ إِنْ كَانُوا صَادِقِينَ﴾ in what they say.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ﴾ that is, without a creator, ﴿أَمْ هُمُ الْخَالِقُونَ﴾ of themselves? A created thing without a creator is inconceivable, and a non-existent thing does not create; so they must have a Creator, and He is Allah the One. Why then do they not affirm His oneness and believe in His Messenger and His Book?

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿أَمْ خَلَقُوا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ None is able to create them but Allah the Creator; why then do they not worship Him? ﴿بَلْ لَا يُوقِنُونَ﴾ in Him; otherwise they would have believed in His Prophet.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿أَمْ عِنْدَهُمْ خَزَائِنُ رَبِّكَ﴾ of prophethood, provision and other things, so that they may single out whomever they wish with whatever they wish? ﴿أَمْ هُمُ الْمُسَيْطِرُونَ﴾ the overpowering tyrants? Its verb is سَيْطَرَ, and like it are بَيْطَرَ and بَيْقَرَ.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ﴾ a means of ascent to heaven, ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ﴾ that is, on it, to the speech of the angels, so that they could dispute with the Prophet, as they claim, if they claim that? ﴿فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ﴾ that is, the one claiming to listen on it, ﴿بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ with a clear, evident proof. And because this claim resembles their claim that the angels are the daughters of Allah, He, Exalted is He, said:

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿أَمْ لَهُ الْبَنَاتُ﴾ that is, by your claim, ﴿وَلَكُمُ الْبَنُونَ﴾? Allah is far above what they claim.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ أَجْرًا﴾ for the religion you have brought them, ﴿فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ﴾ the cost of that ﴿مُثْقَلُونَ﴾ so that they do not submit?

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ﴾ that is, knowledge of it, ﴿فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ﴾ that, so that they could dispute with the Prophet ﷺ about the resurrection and the matters of the Hereafter, as they claim?

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿أَمْ يُرِيدُونَ كَيْدًا﴾ against you, to destroy you in Dār al-Nadwa? ﴿فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هُمُ الْمَكِيدُونَ﴾ the overcome, the destroyed; so Allah protected him from them, then destroyed them at Badr.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ إِلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Him of gods. The interrogative with أَمْ in its places [here] is for denouncing and rebuking.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كِسْفًا﴾ a part ﴿مِنَ السَّمَاءِ سَاقِطًا﴾ upon them, as they said {فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسْفًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ}, that is, as a punishment for them, ﴿يَقُولُوا﴾ this is ﴿سَحَابٌ مَرْكُومٌ﴾ piled up, by which we will be watered; and they would not believe.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ حَتَّى يُلَاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ﴾ they die,

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِي﴾ a badal (substitute) for يَوْمَهُمْ ﴿عَنْهُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ protected from the punishment in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ by their disbelief ﴿عَذَابًا دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ that is, in this world before their death; so they were punished with hunger and drought for seven years, and with killing on the day of Badr; ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that the punishment will descend on them.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ in granting them respite, and let your breast not be constricted; ﴿فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا﴾ within Our sight: We see you and protect you; ﴿وَسَبِّحْ﴾ accompanied ﴿بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ that is, say «سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ», ﴿حِينَ تَقُومُ﴾ from your sleep or from your sitting.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ literally, as well; ﴿وَإِدْبَارَ النُّجُومِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun), that is, after their setting, glorify Him too; or [it means] pray: in the first, the two evening prayers (ʿishāʾayn), and in the second, the dawn prayer (fajr); and it is said: the morning prayer (ṣubḥ).

daas-irab:1-12.t: ﴿وَالطُّورِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم". ﴿وَكِتابٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الطور. ﴿مَسْطُورٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿فِي رَقٍّ﴾ the two are attached to مسطور. ﴿مَنْشُورٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿وَالْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَالسَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَالْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ عَذابَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَواقِعٌ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and واقع is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is the answer to the first oath. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an advanced khabar. ﴿مِنْ دافِعٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and دافع is genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a second khabar of inna. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿تَمُورُ السَّماءُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مَوْراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَتَسِيرُ الْجِبالُ سَيْراً﴾ conjoined to what precedes it, and its i'rab is clear. ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ a particle of resumption, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to an adverb like it. ﴿لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ an adjective of المكذبين. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي خَوْضٍ﴾ the two are attached to يلعبون. ﴿يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.

daas-irab:13-18.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from يومئذ. ﴿يُدَعُّونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلى نارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿دَعًّا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿هذِهِ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿النَّارُ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective of النار. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿بِها﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause) of التي. ﴿أَفَسِحْرٌ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an advanced khabar. ﴿هذا﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ in the sense of bal. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ a particle of negation. ﴿تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿اصْلَوْها﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and hā its mafʿūl (object). ﴿فَاصْبِرُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا تَصْبِرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿سَواءٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "your patience and its absence are alike". ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to سواء. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa). ﴿تُجْزَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿ما﴾ relative, a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila of mā. ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar. ﴿وَنَعِيمٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جنات; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فاكِهِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to فاكهين. ﴿آتاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl. ﴿رَبُّهُمْ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of mā. ﴿وَوَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾ conjoined to آتاهم ربهم. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:19-24.t: ﴿كُلُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of an omitted saying. ﴿وَاشْرَبُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to كلوا. ﴿هَنِيئاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كلوا. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿عَلى سُرُرٍ﴾ the two are attached to the ḥāl. ﴿مَصْفُوفَةٍ﴾ an adjective of سرر. ﴿وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿بِحُورٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿عِينٍ﴾ an adjective of حور; the clause is conjoined to His words في جنات. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its mafʿūl and a postponed fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِإِيمانٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿أَلْحَقْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar of الذين. [Translator's note: the source vowels this word with ḍamma (ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ); as mafʿūl bihi it is ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ.] ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is negating. ﴿أَلَتْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ min is redundant (zāʾida); شيء is genitive in form, accusative in position, a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كُلُّ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿امْرِئٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to رهين. ﴿كَسَبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿رَهِينٌ﴾ the khabar of كل; the verbal clause is the ṣila of mā, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِفاكِهَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَلَحْمٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of لحم. ﴿يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَتَنازَعُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿كَأْساً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا﴾ negating, without governing effect (muhmala). ﴿لَغْوٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; the clause is an adjective of كأس. ﴿وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ﴾ conjoined to لا لغو. ﴿وَيَطُوفُ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿غِلْمانٌ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of غلمان. ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ﴾ كأن, its noun and its khabar. ﴿مَكْنُونٌ﴾ an adjective of لؤلؤ; the clause is an adjective of غلمان.

daas-irab:25-31.t: ﴿وَأَقْبَلَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb. ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿قَبْلُ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿فِي أَهْلِنا﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿مُشْفِقِينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause كنا is the khabar of inna, and the clause إنا is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَمَنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَوَقانا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its mafʿūl (object); the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَذابَ﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿السَّمُومِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ the two are attached to ندعوه; the clause كنا is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause إنا is the object of saying. ﴿نَدْعُوهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is the khabar of كنا. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ two predicates; the nominal clause is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation, and mā is negating, operating like laysa. ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ its noun. ﴿بِنِعْمَةِ﴾ the two are attached to the negation conveyed by mā. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِكاهِنٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position as the khabar of mā. ﴿وَلا مَجْنُونٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; the clause ما أنت is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of bal. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿شاعِرٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو شاعر"; the nominal clause is the object of saying. ﴿نَتَرَبَّصُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is an adjective. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿رَيْبَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْمَنُونِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَرَبَّصُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿فَإِنِّي﴾ the fāʾ is for causation, and inna and its noun. ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿مِنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ﴾ the khabar of inna; the nominal clause is an explanation of cause.

daas-irab:32-38.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَأْمُرُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿أَحْلامُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِهذا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿هُمْ قَوْمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿طاغُونَ﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَقَوَّلَهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَلْيَأْتُوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the implied (muqaddar) condition. ﴿بِحَدِيثٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِثْلِهِ﴾ an adjective. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional, governing the jussive. ﴿كانُوا صادِقِينَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is initial. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿خُلِقُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿مِنْ غَيْرِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿هُمُ الْخالِقُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿خَلَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُوقِنُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿عِنْدَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿خَزائِنُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿هُمُ الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿سُلَّمٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is an adjective of سلم. ﴿فَلْيَأْتِ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. ﴿مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective of سلطان; the verbal clause is the apodosis of a condition that does not govern the jussive.

daas-irab:39-42.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَهُ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿الْبَناتُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَكُمُ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿الْبَنُونَ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَسْئَلُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَجْراً﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ a conjunction and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿مُثْقَلُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿عِنْدَهُمُ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿الْغَيْبُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ a conjunction and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَكْتُبُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يُرِيدُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿كَيْداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَالَّذِينَ﴾ a particle of resumption and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿هُمُ الْمَكِيدُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين.

daas-irab:43-45.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿إِلهٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ an adjective. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبحان. ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and in is a conditional particle governing the jussive. ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿كِسْفاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of كسفا. ﴿ساقِطاً﴾ a second adjective of كسفا; the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿يَقُولُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is not joined with the fāʾ. ﴿سَحابٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَرْكُومٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit and genitive. ﴿يُلاقُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an concealed after حتى, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿يَوْمَهُمُ﴾ its mafʿūl; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb ذرهم. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective of يومهم. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿يُصْعَقُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila of الذي.

daas-irab:46-49.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from يومهم. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُغْنِي﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كَيْدُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَلا﴾ a conjunction, and lā is negating. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of هم, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and inna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَذاباً﴾ the postponed noun of inna. ﴿دُونَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾ lākinna and its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of lākinna, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاصْبِرْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِحُكْمِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَإِنَّكَ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation, and inna and its noun. ﴿بِأَعْيُنِنا﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar of inna; the nominal clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿وَسَبِّحْ﴾ a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِحَمْدِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿حِينَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿تَقُومُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what follows them. ﴿فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl (object); the fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَإِدْبارَ﴾ a conjunction, and إدبار is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿النُّجُومِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

dervis-irab:39-49.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَغْرَمٍ) The maghram is that a person takes upon himself what is not incumbent on him.
(كِسْفاً) A piece; it is also said to be «كِسَفاً», whose singular is «كِسْفَة», like «سِدْرَة» and «سِدْر».
(مَرْكُومٌ) Placed one part on top of another.

* I'rab:
(أَمْ لَهُ الْبَناتُ وَلَكُمُ الْبَنُونَ) «له» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «البنات» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ولكم البنون» is conjoined to «له البنات».
(أَمْ تَسْئَلُهُمْ أَجْراً فَهُمْ مِنْ مَغْرَمٍ مُثْقَلُونَ) «تسألهم» is an imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and a first direct object; «أجرا» is the second direct object. The «فاء» is a conjunction; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ; «من مغرم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مثقلون»; and «مثقلون» is the khabar.
(أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ) The adverbial is attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and «الغيب» is a postponed mubtadaʾ. The «فاء» is a conjunction; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause «يكتبون» is the khabar.
(أَمْ يُرِيدُونَ كَيْداً فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هُمُ الْمَكِيدُونَ) «يريدون» is a nominative imperfect verb, the «واو» is the agent, and «كيدا» is the direct object. The «فاء» is a conjunction; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ — this is a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, which has been pointed out before; the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila (relative clause). «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and «المكيدون» is its khabar, and the nominal clause is the khabar of «الذين».
(أَمْ لَهُمْ إِلهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ) «لهم» is a fronted khabar and «إله» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «غير الله» is an adjective of «إله»; «سبحان الله» is accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); «عمّا» is attached to «سبحان»; and the clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position, because «ما» is either a relative noun or a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle.
(وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كِسْفاً مِنَ السَّماءِ ساقِطاً يَقُولُوا سَحابٌ مَرْكُومٌ) The «واو» is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «يروا» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the «نون», and the «واو» is the agent; «كسفا» is the direct object; «من السماء» is an adjective of «كسفا»; «يقولوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «سحاب» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; and «مركوم» is an adjective of «سحاب».
(فَذَرْهُمْ حَتَّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ) The «فاء» is the «fāʾ al-faṣīḥa» (the eloquent fāʾ), because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, the implied sense being: "if they have reached this limit in disbelief and obstinacy, and it has become clear that they will not turn back from disbelief, then leave them until they die upon it". «ذرهم» is an imperative verb, a latent agent, and a direct object; «حتى» is a particle of limit and genitive; «يلاقوا» is an imperfect verb, jussive through an implied «أن» after «حتى» [Translator's note: the source says «مجزوم» (jussive); after «حتى» the verb is normally subjunctive (manṣūb), and the verb here has no visible ending to show either]; «يومهم» is the direct object; «الذي» is an adjective of «يومهم»; «فيه» is attached to His words «يصعقون»; and the clause «يصعقون» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «الذي». «يصعقون» is passive, from the triliteral «صعق» or from the quadriliteral «أصعق», the meaning being that others made them swoon; it was also read «يَصْعَقُون» with the active voice, meaning "they die from the severity of the terrors".
(يَوْمَ لا يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئاً وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ) «يوم» is a badal (substitute) for «يومهم»; the clause «لا يغني» is in the position of the genitive, through the adverbial's being annexed to it; «عنهم» is attached to «يغني»; «كيدهم» is the agent of «يغني»; «شيئا» is a direct object or an absolute object; the «واو» is a conjunction, «لا» is negative, «هم» is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause «ينصرون» is the khabar.
(وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا عَذاباً دُونَ ذلِكَ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) The «واو» is resumptive; «إن» is a particle resembling the verb; «للذين» is its fronted khabar; the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila of the relative noun [Translator's note: the source says «كفروا», although the verse has «ظلموا»]; «عذابا» is the postponed noun of «إن»; «دون» is an adverbial attached to an omitted adjective of «عذابا»; «ذلك» is a demonstrative, genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. As for «ولكن», the «واو» is a conjunction or circumstantial, and «لكن» is a particle resembling the verb, for rectification; «أكثرهم» is its noun, and the clause «لا يعلمون» is the khabar of «لكن».
(وَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنا وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ) The «واو» is a conjunction; «اصبر» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on sukūn, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; «لحكم ربك» is attached to «اصبر»; the «فاء» gives a reason; «إن» and its noun; «بأعيننا» is the khabar of «إنك», i.e. "within Our sight, where We see you and guard you". The plural of «العين» is used because the pronoun is in plural form. «سبّح» is conjoined to «اصبر»; «بحمد ربك» is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "joined with the praise of your Lord"; «حين» is an adverbial attached to «سبّح»; and the clause «تقوم» is in the position of the genitive, through the adverbial's being annexed to it.
(وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَإِدْبارَ النُّجُومِ) The «واو» is a conjunction; «من الليل» is attached to «سبّحه»; «سبّحه» is an imperative verb, a latent agent, and a direct object; «إدبار النجوم» is a maṣdar that stands in for the adverbial, and its ruling will come in the section on Benefits.

* Benefits:
What stands in for the adverbial is what is genitive through the annexation of one of the two adverbials to it, after which the muḍāf (the first term of the construct) is omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi is put in its place after its omission. Most often this muḍāf ilayhi which stands in for the omitted muḍāf is a maṣdar, as in «جئتك صلاة العصر» ("I came to you at the time of the afternoon prayer") or «قدوم الحاج» ("at the arrival of the pilgrim"): «صلاة» and «قدوم» are both mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), accusative with the accusative of an adverb of time, because when they stood in for time, the nominal status of time befell them, so they became accusative as it is accusative. The original is «وقت صلاة العصر» and «وقت قدوم الحاج». Of this kind is «وإدبار النجوم», i.e. the time of their setting. Among their sayings is «لا أكلمه القارظين» ("I will not speak to him [until] the two qāriẓs [return]"), the original being «مدة غيبة القارظين» (the duration of the absence of the two qāriẓs): «مدة» was omitted and «غيبة» put in its place, then «غيبة» was omitted and «القارظين» put in its place. It is the dual of «قارظ», who is the one who gathers the «قَرَظ» (with fatḥa on the «قاف» and the «راء»), which is something with which hides are tanned. Al-Jawharī said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "«لا آتيك أو يئوب القارظ العنزي»" ("I will not come to you until the qāriẓ of ʿAnaza returns"), and they are two qāriẓs, both of ʿAnaza, who went out seeking «القرظ» and did not return, and their absence was prolonged.

dervis-irab:1-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطُّورِ) A well-known mountain. It was said that al-Ṭūr is any mountain on which fruit-bearing trees grow, and one on which nothing grows is not a ṭūr. Al-Mubarrad said: "Every mountain is called a ṭūr; but when alif and lām of definiteness enter, it refers to one particular thing."
(مَسْطُورٍ) Consistently written in ordered lines, in arranged letters. In al-Mukhtār: "Al-saṭr is a row of something; one says 'he built a saṭr'. Al-saṭr is also the line and the writing; it is originally a maṣdar and its verb pattern is naṣara; also saṭar with two fatḥas; the plural is asṭār, like sabab and asbāb; the plural of the plural is asāṭīr; and the plural of al-saṭr is asṭur and suṭūr, like aflus and fulūs."
(رَقٍّ) Al-raqq, with fatḥa or kasra, is thin skin on which one writes, and its plural is ruqūq; al-riqq, with kasra, is the owned slave. Al-Rāghib's text: "Al-raqq is anything written on, whether skin or otherwise, and it is with fatḥa on the rāʾ according to the better-known view, though kasra is permissible, as it was read in an irregular reading. As for al-riqq, which is the ownership of slaves, it is with kasra only." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-raqq is the leaf; it was also said to be the skin on which is written the book in which deeds are recorded."
(الْمَسْجُورِ) Filled with water.
(تَمُورُ) It shakes, comes and goes. In al-Mukhtār: "Māra (verb pattern qāla): it moved and went; and from it His saying, the Exalted, «يوم تمور السماء مورا». Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it surges with a surging; Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash said: it tilts over."
(اصْلَوْها) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Ṣaliya bi-l-nār and ṣaliyahā, yaṣlā (verb pattern taʿiba): he felt its heat; al-ṣalāʾ, on the pattern of kitāb, is the heat of fire; and ṣalaytu l-laḥma uṣlīhi (verb pattern ramā): I roasted the meat."
(يُدَعُّونَ) Al-daʿʿ is pushing. It was said to be that the hands are shackled to the necks and the sides are gathered to the feet, and then they are pushed violently on their faces. In al-Mukhtār: "Daʿʿahu: he pushed him (verb pattern radda); and from it His saying, the Exalted, «فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم»."

* I'rab:
(وَالطُّورِ وَكِتابٍ مَسْطُورٍ فِي رَقٍّ مَنْشُورٍ) The wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; they are five oaths, whose response is «إن عذاب ربك لواقع». The first wāw is for the oath and the wāws after it are conjunctions, or each of them is for an oath; فِي رَقٍّ is attached to مَسْطُورٍ or is another adjective of كِتابٍ. (وَالْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ وَالسَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ وَالْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ) Conjoined to His saying «والطور», or each of them is an independent oath, and the response to all of them is His saying: (إِنَّ عَذابَ رَبِّكَ لَواقِعٌ) inna and its noun, the shifted lām, and وَاقِعٌ is the khabar of inna. (ما لَهُ مِنْ دافِعٍ) مَا is negative; لَهُ is a fronted khabar; مِنْ is a redundant preposition and دَافِعٍ is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ; this sentence is a second khabar of inna or an adjective of وَاقِعٌ. (يَوْمَ تَمُورُ السَّماءُ مَوْراً) The adverb is attached to وَاقِعٌ, that is, "the punishment will befall on that day", and the negative clause is parenthetical between the operator and what it governs; it was also said that the adverb is attached to دَافِعٍ. The clause تَمُورُ السَّماءُ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and مَوْراً is an absolute object. (وَتَسِيرُ الْجِبالُ سَيْراً) The sentence is conjoined to the clause تَمُورُ السَّماءُ مَوْراً. (فَوَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, since the speech has the sense of requital, and the implied form is "when what was mentioned occurs, woe to those who deny Allah and His Messenger"; وَيْلٌ is a mubtadaʾ, and commencing with it was permissible because of the sense of supplication it contains; يَوْمَئِذٍ is an adverb accusative by وَيْلٌ, with إِذْ an adverb annexed to a like adverb, the tanwīn being a substitute for a clause; and لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ is the khabar of وَيْلٌ. (الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي خَوْضٍ يَلْعَبُونَ) الَّذِينَ is an adjective of الْمُكَذِّبِينَ; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ, فِي خَوْضٍ is attached to يَلْعَبُونَ, and the clause يَلْعَبُونَ is their khabar; the sentence has no position because it is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ. (يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلى نارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا) The adverb is a badal from يَوْمَ تَمُورُ السَّماءُ مَوْراً or from يَوْمَئِذٍ before it; the clause يُدَعُّونَ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; يُدَعُّونَ is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil; إِلى نارِ جَهَنَّمَ is attached to يُدَعُّونَ; and دَعًّا is an absolute object. (هذِهِ النَّارُ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ بِها تُكَذِّبُونَ) The sentence is accusative as the object of an omitted saying, that is, "it will be said to them: this"; هذِهِ is a mubtadaʾ and النَّارُ the khabar; الَّتِي is an adjective, and the clause كُنْتُمْ is the ṣila of الَّتِي; kāna and its noun; بِها is attached to تُكَذِّبُونَ, and the clause تُكَذِّبُونَ is the khabar of كُنْتُمْ. (أَفَسِحْرٌ هذا أَمْ أَنْتُمْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; the fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted element, the implied form being "you used to say of the revelation, 'this is sorcery'; is this sorcery?", meaning: is this thing too, which bears it out, sorcery? and the fāʾ has conveyed this meaning. سِحْرٌ is a fronted khabar and هذا a postponed mubtadaʾ; أَمْ may be munqaṭiʿa (disconnected) in the sense of "rather", because the speech is complete at His saying «أفسحر هذا», and then He said «أم أنتم», that is, "rather, you do not see"; or it may be muttaṣila (connected), that is, "neither of the two is established, so it is established that you have been resurrected and that what you see is true", which is a severe reproach and a dreadful mockery. أَنْتُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا تُبْصِرُونَ the khabar. (اصْلَوْها فَاصْبِرُوا أَوْ لا تَصْبِرُوا سَواءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ) اصْلَوْها: an imperative verb, agent and direct object; the fāʾ is a conjunction, and اصْبِرُوا an imperative verb and agent; أَوْ is a conjunction, lā prohibitive, and تَصْبِرُوا an imperfect verb jussive by lā; سَواءٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "your patience and leaving it are equal", and عَلَيْكُمْ is attached to سَواءٌ. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to parse it as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, "equal for you are the two things", and Abū Ḥayyān followed him; nothing prevents that, because the sense of equalising contained in سَواءٌ gave it a benefit that justified parsing it as a mubtadaʾ. (إِنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) innamā: the particle that restrains (kāffa) and the one restrained; تُجْزَوْنَ is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil; مَا is a relative noun, a second direct object, and the clause كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ is the ṣila; kāna and its noun, and the clause تَعْمَلُونَ is its khabar; and the clause innamā tujzawna is a justification of the equality.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya) in His saying «الذين هم في خوض يلعبون»:
The origin of khawḍ is to be in water; one says "khāḍa l-māʾ", he entered it; then it came to predominate for plunging into falsehood and other things. Lying and rushing into falsehood are likened to a deep pool which the player wades into. One says "khāḍa l-ghamarāt", that is, he plunged into it; "khāḍa fī l-ḥadīth", he went on at length in it; "khāḍa l-jawādu fī l-maydān", the steed frolicked on the field; and one says "he wades through deaths" (yakhūḍu l-manāyā), that is, he throws himself into perils; and "he wades through the night" (yakhūḍu l-layl), that is, he gropes about in it, heedless of terrors. In the language there are nouns on which particular meanings came to predominate, such as iḥḍār (bringing forward), which is general for everything and then came to predominate in use for bringing forward for punishment; the Exalted said: «لكنت من المحضرين». Its parallel among the predominant nouns is dābba, which came to predominate for four-legged creatures, and qawm, which came to predominate for men. The metaphor here is explicit.
2- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): كِتاب was made indefinite in His saying «وكتاب مسطور» because it is a particular book from among the genus of books, as in His saying: «ونفس وما سواها».
3- Self-imposed constraint (al-iltizām): in His saying «والطور وكتاب مسطور» is the art of iltizām, to which reference has already been made, for the ṭāʾ has come before the wāw of ridf as an obligatory element.

dervis-irab:17-28.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فاكِهِينَ) Enjoying comfort and delight. Al-Zajjāj and al-Farrāʾ said: fākihīn means admiring what their Lord has given them. In al-Mukhtār: "Fakiha l-rajulu (verb pattern salima), fa-huwa fakih, when he is of good spirit and humorous. Al-fakih is also the arrogant, insolent one. It was read «ونعمة كانوا فيها فكهين», that is, 'insolent', and «فاكهين», that is, 'enjoying comfort'. Al-mufākaha is jesting; tafakkaha means he was astonished, and it was also said, he regretted; Allah the Exalted said: «فظلتم تفكهون», that is, 'you regret'; and tafakkaha bi-l-shayʾ means he enjoyed it."
(بِحُورٍ) Al-ḥūr is the plural of ḥawrāʾ, from al-ḥawar, which is the intense whiteness of the eye in the intense blackness of it.
(عِينٍ) Al-ʿīn is the plural of ʿaynāʾ, which is a woman with wide eyes.
(أَلَتْناهُمْ) We diminished them. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Alata l-shayʾa altan (verb pattern ḍaraba): it diminished; it is also used transitively, so one says alatahu."
(السَّمُومِ) Fire, because it enters the pores; it is originally the hot wind that penetrates the pores; the plural is samāʾim. Thaʿlab said: al-samūm is the intensity of heat and the intensity of cold in the daytime. Abū ʿUbayda said: al-samūm is by day, though it may occur at night, and al-ḥarr is by night, though it may occur by day. It was said that the origin of al-samūm is from al-samm, which is the outlet of breath, so every aperture is a samm; or from al-samm, which kills (poison).

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ) inna and its noun; فِي جَنَّاتٍ is its khabar, and نَعِيمٍ is conjoined to جَنَّاتٍ. The speech is resumptive, brought to convey glad tidings to the pious; it may also be a continuation of what is said to the disbelievers, to increase their vexation and bring regret into their hearts. (فاكِهِينَ بِما آتاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ وَوَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَذابَ الْجَحِيمِ) فاكِهِينَ is a ḥāl, and بِما is attached to فاكِهِينَ; مَا is a relative noun referring to the fruits that are in Paradise, that is, "taking delight in the fruit of Paradise"; the bāʾ may also mean "in", that is, "in what He has given them of fruits and other things"; and مَا may also be maṣdariyya. آتاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ is a past verb with a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; وَوَقاهُمْ is conjoined to the ṣila, that is, "delighting in their Lord's giving and in His protecting them from the punishment of Hell". The wāw may be circumstantial, in which case the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with qad implied according to those who require it to accompany a past verb occurring as a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be conjoined to جَنَّاتٍ. عَذابَ الْجَحِيمِ is a second direct object. (كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) The sentence is the content of an omitted saying; هَنِيئاً is a ḥāl or an absolute object, being in the sense of a maṣdar. Full discussion of هَنِيئاً has been given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. بِما is attached to كُلُوا or اشْرَبُوا, and the clause كُنْتُمْ is a ṣila; kāna and its noun, and the clause تَعْمَلُونَ is the khabar of كُنْتُمْ. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that the bāʾ be redundant and مَا be the agent of هَنِيئاً, but the redundancy of the bāʾ is not analogical except in the agent of kafā, and Abū Ḥayyān rejected this of him. (مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى سُرُرٍ مَصْفُوفَةٍ وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ بِحُورٍ عِينٍ) مُتَّكِئِينَ is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in His saying فِي جَنَّاتٍ, that is, "being in gardens, reclining", or from the agent of كُلُوا, or from the object of آتاهُمْ, or from the object of وَقاهُمْ; عَلى سُرُرٍ is attached to مُتَّكِئِينَ, and مَصْفُوفَةٍ is an adjective of سُرُرٍ; the wāw is a conjunction, and زَوَّجْناهُمْ is a verb, agent and direct object; بِحُورٍ is attached to زَوَّجْناهُمْ, and عِينٍ is an adjective of حُورٍ. (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ بِإِيمانٍ أَلْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ)
There are three views on the wāw, which we set out below, then we indicate where the preponderance lies: 1- It is resumptive; الَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is the clause أَلْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ; this is the view of most of the exegetes and parsers. 2- Abū l-Baqāʾ said: it is accusative by an omitted verb, the implied form being "and We honoured those who believed". 3- Al-Zamakhsharī said: وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا is conjoined to حُورٍ عِينٍ, that is, "We paired them with the ḥūr and with those who believed", meaning with companions and fellows from among them, as in His saying, the Exalted, «إخوانا على سرر متقابلين», so they enjoy at one time the dalliance of the ḥūr and at another the companionship of their believing brothers. Abū Ḥayyān rebutted al-Zamakhsharī, saying: "No one imagined that His saying «والذين آمنوا» is conjoined to «بحور عين» other than this man, and it is a non-Arab imagining contrary to the understanding of the Arab", and we do not hesitate to side with Abū Ḥayyān in his rebuttal. The clause آمَنُوا is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ; وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ is conjoined to آمَنُوا; بِإِيمانٍ is a ḥāl from ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ, that is, "the offspring being accompanied by faith"; and the clause أَلْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ is the khabar of الَّذِينَ. (وَما أَلَتْناهُمْ مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ بِما كَسَبَ رَهِينٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; أَلَتْناهُمْ is a verb, agent and direct object; مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ is a ḥāl; مِنْ is a redundant preposition and شَيْءٍ is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is a second object; كُلُّ is a mubtadaʾ and امْرِئٍ its muḍāf ilayhi; in بِما, the bāʾ is a preposition and مَا is relative or maṣdariyya, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to رَهِينٌ, and رَهِينٌ is the khabar of كُلُّ. (وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ بِفاكِهَةٍ وَلَحْمٍ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ) وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ is conjoined to what preceded; بِفاكِهَةٍ is attached to أَمْدَدْناهُمْ; وَلَحْمٍ is conjoined to فاكِهَةٍ; مِمَّا is an adjective, and the clause يَشْتَهُونَ is the ṣila of the relative. (يَتَنازَعُونَ فِيها كَأْساً لا لَغْوٌ فِيها وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ) The sentence is resumptive; it was also said to be accusative as a ḥāl from the object of أَمْدَدْناهُمْ. يَتَنازَعُونَ is an imperfect verb and agent, and فِيها is attached to يَتَنازَعُونَ; كَأْساً is a direct object; lā is the lā of generic negation, ignored for its repetition; لَغْوٌ is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is فِيها, and وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ is conjoined to it; commencing with it was made permissible by the negation preceding it. The meaning of "they contend over the cup" is that they pull it back and forth in playful pulling, since the people of this world have a pleasure in that; it was also said that يَتَنازَعُونَ means they hand it to one another. Al-Akhṭal said: "I contended with him over the fine, cool wine, when the cocks had crowed and the time of the night traveller's halt had come."
(وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ غِلْمانٌ لَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ مَكْنُونٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; يَطُوفُ is a nominative imperfect verb, and عَلَيْهِمْ is attached to يَطُوفُ; غِلْمانٌ is the agent of يَطُوفُ, and لَهُمْ is an adjective of غِلْمانٌ; ka-anna and its noun, and لُؤْلُؤٌ is its khabar, and مَكْنُونٌ an adjective of لُؤْلُؤٌ; the clause كَأَنَّهُمْ is a second adjective. (وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; أَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ is a verb and agent, and عَلى بَعْضٍ is attached to أَقْبَلَ
and the clause يَتَساءَلُونَ is a ḥāl. (قالُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ فِي أَهْلِنا مُشْفِقِينَ) قالُوا is a verb and agent; inna and its noun, and the clause كُنَّا is its khabar, and the clause إِنَّا كُنَّا is the content of the saying; قَبْلُ is an adverb indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording and not in meaning, and the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl; مُشْفِقِينَ is the khabar of كُنَّا. (فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا وَوَقانا عَذابَ السَّمُومِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; مَنَّ اللَّهُ is a verb and agent, and عَلَيْنا is attached to مَنَّ; وَوَقانا is conjoined to مَنَّ, and عَذابَ السَّمُومِ is a second direct object. (إِنَّا كُنَّا مِنْ قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ) inna and its noun; kāna and its noun; مِنْ قَبْلُ is a ḥāl; the clause نَدْعُوهُ is the khabar of كُنَّا, and the clause كُنَّا is the khabar of إِنَّا; inna and its noun; هُوَ is a separating pronoun or ʿimād; الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ are two khabars of inna; and the clause إِنَّهُ is a justification with no position.

* Rhetoric:
The unrestricted, concise simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal al-mujmal): in His saying «كأنهم لؤلؤ مكنون» there is a tashbīh mursal mujmal. He likened the youths to pearls hidden in their shells, because it is finer and purer, or because it is stored away and only what is precious and highly valued is stored. The ṣadaf of the pearl is its covering, the singular being ṣadafa, like qaṣaba and qaṣab.

* Benefits:
When the lā of generic negation is repeated, five forms are permissible with it: 1- Both nouns are indeclinable, on the basis that it operates the operation of inna in both, as in: لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله.
2- Both are nominative, on the basis that it is ignored, so what follows it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, as in: لا لغو فيها ولا تأثيم. And the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
ماذا تقول لأفراخ بذي مرخ ... زغب الحواصل لا ماء ولا شجر
(What will you say to the chicks in Dhū Marakh, with downy crops, where there is no water and no tree?)
3- The first is indeclinable on the fatḥa and the second nominative, as in the saying of Abū l-Ṭayyib:
لا خيل عندك تهديها ولا مال ... فليسعد النطق إن لم تسعد الحال
(You have no horses to give as gifts and no wealth; so let speech help, if circumstance does not.)
4- The first nominative and the second indeclinable on the fatḥa, as in:
فلا لغو ولا تأثيم فيها ... وما فاهوا به أبدا مقيم
(There is no idle talk and no sinning in it, and what they utter there is forever abiding.)
5- The first indeclinable on the fatḥa and the second accusative, by conjunction upon the position of the noun of lā, as in:
لا نسب اليوم ولا خلة ... اتسع الخرق على الراقع
(No lineage today and no friendship; the tear has grown wider than the patcher can mend.)

dervis-irab:29-38.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الكاهن) The one who claims to report the truth by way of incantations; al-kahāna is the attribute of the kāhin (soothsayer).
(نَتَرَبَّصُ) Tarabbuṣ is waiting for a thing, for a change of its state into its opposite.
(الْمَنُونِ) Fate and death, from manna-hu when he cut it, because death is a cutter; and its rayb (misgivings) are the events that cause misgiving when they come. He said:
تربص بها ريب المنون لعلها ... سيهلك عنها بعلها أو سيجنح
(Wait out the misfortunes of fate for her; perhaps her husband will perish and leave her, or he will incline away.)
(أَحْلامُهُمْ) Their minds. Aḥlām is the plural of ḥilm, which is the forbearance to which reason and wisdom call. In al-Qāmūs: "Al-ḥilm, with kasra, is deliberateness and intellect; the plural is aḥlām and ḥulūm; and from it «أم تأمرهم أحلامهم بهذا»."
(الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ) The plural of al-musayṭir, who is the overpowering, dominating one, from sayṭara ʿalayhi when he watched over him and guarded him or subdued him. Abū ʿUbayda related "sayṭarta ʿalayya" when you take me as a servant. No noun of the pattern mufayʿil has come in the speech of the Arabs except five words:
muhaymin, muḥaymir, mubayṭir, musayṭir and mubayqir; muḥaymir is the name of a mountain and the rest are names of agents. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "Al-musayṭir and al-muṣayṭir is the one set over a thing to supervise it, to look after its property and to record its work; its origin is from al-saṭr, because books are written in lines (yusaṭṭar)."

* I'rab:
(فَذَكِّرْ فَما أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِكاهِنٍ وَلا مَجْنُونٍ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; ذَكِّرْ is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, implied "أنت"; the fāʾ gives the reason; مَا is the Ḥijāzī negative and أَنْتَ is its noun. As for بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ, this preposition and its genitive noun may be attached to the sense of negation contained in مَا, in which case the bāʾ is causal, which is the highest of the views, and the meaning is "soothsaying and madness are negated from you by reason of the favour of your Lord upon you", as you say "I am not in straitened circumstances, thanks (bi-ḥamd) to Allah and His enrichment" [Translator's note: the source reads «بحمد بالله»; «بحمد الله» is evidently intended]. Abū l-Baqāʾ said that the phrase with the bāʾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and its operator is بِكاهِنٍ or مَجْنُونٍ, the implied form being "you are not a soothsayer nor a madman, while accompanied by the favour of your Lord"; on this it is an inseparable ḥāl and the bāʾ is of accompaniment. It was also said the bāʾ is for the oath and نِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ is what is sworn by, interposed between the noun of مَا and its khabar, so it is attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is "أقسم", with the response omitted, the implied form being "By the favour of your Lord, you are not a soothsayer nor a madman"; and this is the weakest of them. (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ شاعِرٌ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ) أَمْ is munqaṭiʿa in the sense of "rather", and it is mentioned here fifteen times, all of them binding arguments to which the addressees have no answer. يَقُولُونَ is a nominative imperfect verb; شاعِرٌ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the clause نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ is an adjective of شاعِرٌ, and بِهِ is attached to نَتَرَبَّصُ; رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ is a direct object. (قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا فَإِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ) قُلْ is an imperative whose agent is latent, implied "أنت"; تَرَبَّصُوا is an imperative indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the agent; the fāʾ gives the reason for the command, whose intent is threat; inna and its noun; مَعَكُمْ is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl; مِنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ is the khabar of إِنِّي; and the clause تَرَبَّصُوا is the content of the saying. (أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلامُهُمْ بِهذا أَمْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طاغُونَ) أَمْ is a conjunction in the sense of "rather", and what was said of it has gone before; تَأْمُرُهُمْ is an imperfect verb with a fronted direct object; أَحْلامُهُمْ is the agent, and بِهذا is attached to تَأْمُرُهُمْ; أَمْ is a conjunction, هُمْ a mubtadaʾ, قَوْمٌ the khabar, and طاغُونَ an adjective. (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُ بَلْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) تَقَوَّلَهُ is a past verb with a direct object, and the agent is latent, implied "هو". (فَلْيَأْتُوا بِحَدِيثٍ مِثْلِهِ إِنْ كانُوا صادِقِينَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, that is, "if they say he fabricated it, that is, invented it, then let them bring"; the lām is the lām of command, and يَأْتُوا is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command, the wāw being the agent; بِحَدِيثٍ is attached to يَأْتُوا, and مِثْلِهِ is an adjective of حَدِيثٍ; إِنْ is conditional, and kāna with its noun and khabar; the apodosis of إِنْ is omitted, indicated by what precedes, that is, "if they are truthful in this saying, let them bring". (أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ الْخالِقُونَ) Conjoined to what preceded; مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ is attached to خُلِقُوا; and أَمْ هُمُ الْخالِقُونَ is a mubtadaʾ and khabar. (أَمْ خَلَقُوا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بَلْ لا يُوقِنُونَ) Conjoined to what preceded. (أَمْ عِنْدَهُمْ خَزائِنُ رَبِّكَ أَمْ هُمُ الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ) The adverb is attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar, and خَزائِنُ is a postponed mubtadaʾ; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ the khabar. (أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ) لَهُمْ is a fronted khabar and سُلَّمٌ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause يَسْتَمِعُونَ is an adjective of سُلَّمٌ, and فِيهِ is attached to يَسْتَمِعُونَ. فَلْيَأْتِ: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, the implied form being "if they claim that, let ... come"; the lām is the lām of command and يَأْتِ is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command; مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ is the agent, بِسُلْطانٍ is attached to يَأْتِ, and مُبِينٍ is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «أم تأمرهم أحلامهم بهذا» there is a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī), for the commanding is attributed to the minds. The Arabs used to pride themselves on their intellects, so Allah disparaged them in that they did not yield for them knowledge of truth and falsehood. It may be considered an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) if likening is intended, and every majāz ʿaqlī may be an istiʿāra makniyya, but not conversely.
2- In His saying «نتربص به ريب المنون» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), for rayb was applied to events, and rayb is doubt; events were likened to doubt because they neither last nor remain in one state.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَٱلطُّورِ﴾.
He swore by it; it is the mountain in Midian beside which Allah, Majestic and Mighty, spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, directly.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فِي رَقٍّ مَّنْشُورٍ﴾.
«الرَّق» means the scrolls that will be brought out to the children of Adam: one taking his book in his right hand, and another taking his book in his left hand.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْمَعْمُورِ﴾.
A house that Adam, may Allah bless him, built; it was raised up in the days of the Flood, and it is in the sixth heaven, directly opposite the Kaaba.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَٱلْبَحْرِ ٱلْمَسْجُورِ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say: kindled with fire. And «المسجور» in the speech of the Arabs means: filled.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿يَوْمَ تَمُورُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ مَوْراً﴾.
It will revolve with what is in it, and the mountains will move off the face of the earth, so that they and the earth become level.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ ﴾.
They will be shoved. Likewise His saying: ﴿فَذَلِكَ الَّذِى يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ﴾.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فَاكِهِينَ بِمَآ آتَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾.
Delighted with what their Lord has given them.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَٱتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم﴾: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read it: (وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ). ﴿أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ in the singular.
He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: Qays and al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm — al-Mufaḍḍal said: from ʿAlqama, from ʿAbd Allāh; and Qays said: from a man, from ʿAbd Allāh — he said: A man recited to ʿAbd Allāh: "وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاتّبَعهم ذُرِّيَاتُهم بإِيمانٍ أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّاتِهم". He said: ʿAbd Allāh began reciting it in the singular. He said: until he had repeated it to him about twenty times, without saying "It is not as he says". Al-Ḥasan read both of them in the plural, and some of the people of the Ḥijāz read the first in the singular and the second in the plural. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿وَٱتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم﴾, it is said: when the people of Paradise enter Paradise, if the father is of a higher rank than his son, his son is raised to him; and if the child is of higher rank, his father is raised to him. [57/ا] And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمَآ أَلَتْنَاهُمْ﴾.
«الألْت» means diminishing. There is another dialectal form of it: (وما لِتْناهم من عَملِهم من شىء), and it is so in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh and of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. The poet said:
أبلغْ بنى ثُمَلٍ عنِّى مُغَلْغَلَة * جَهْدَ الرسالةِ لا أَلْتاً ولا كذِبا
(Convey from me to the Banū Thumal a far-travelling message, the message in full, with no diminishing and no lie.)
He means: no diminishing and no adding. Another said:
وليلةٍ ذات نَدىً سَرَيتُ * ولم يَلتْنى عن سُرَاها لَيْتُ
(Many a dewy night I have travelled, and no holding back (layt) kept me from travelling it.)
«اللَّيْت» here is a maṣdar (verbal noun): no deficiency in me and no inability for it turned me away from it.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ﴾.
«إِنَّه»: ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan read it (إِنَّه) with a kasra on the alif, and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī and Nāfiʿ read it (أنَّه). Whoever gives it a kasra begins a new sentence (istaʾnafa); whoever gives it a fatḥa means: «we used to call upon Him because He is the Beneficent, the Merciful», and that is a good reading. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-Kisāʾī reads (أنَّه) with a fatḥa, while I read it with a kasra; I only said "good" because al-Kisāʾī read it so.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ ٱلْمَنُونِ ﴾.
The afflictions of time, so that he will be kept busy away from you and his companions will scatter; or the lifespan of his forefathers, for we know their lifespans.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلاَمُهُمْ بِهَـٰذَآ﴾.
«الأحلام» in this place means minds and intellects.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ٱلْمُصَيْطِرُونَ﴾, and ﴿لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ﴾.
[57/ب] It is written with ṣād, and it is read both with sīn and with ṣād. Al-Kisāʾī read it with sīn. Similar to it are «بصطة» and «بسطة»: some of them are written with ṣād and some with sīn, and the reading is with sīn in «بَسْطة» and «يَبْسُط» — and all of that, I believe he said, is correct.
Al-Farrāʾ said: in the codices (maṣāḥif), in al-Baqara it is written «بَسْطةً», and in al-Aʿrāf «بصطةً» with ṣād, and in the rest of the Qurʾān it is written with sīn.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يُلاَقُواْ يَوْمَهُمُ﴾ with the alif. Some read (يَلْقَوْا), but «الملاقاة» is the more eloquent Arabic, and both are good.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ﴾: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it (يَصعقون) [and the people of the Ḥijāz (يُصعقون)], and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it (يَصعقون) with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, like al-Aʿmash.
«[Translator's note: the source attributes «يَصعقون» (with fatḥa) to ʿĀṣim; in the received transmission ʿĀṣim reads «يُصعقون» with a ḍamma.]»
The Arabs say «صُعِق الرجُلُ» and «صَعِق», and «سُعِد» and «سَعِدَ»; these are dialectal forms, all of them correct.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: (والطور) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] Sworn by (muqsam bihi), genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied "I swear".

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The preposition «في رق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {مَسْطُورٍ}.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (إن عذاب ربك لواقع) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (ما له من دافع) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a second khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; «دافع» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «فويل للمكذبين» is resumptive; «يومئذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ويل»; the preposition «للمكذبين» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «ويل».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of {لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ}, and the clause «يلعبون» is a second khabar (predicate) of «هم».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «هذه النار» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of an implied [saying]; the preposition «بها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تكذبون».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «أفسحر هذا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying); «سحر» is the khabar (predicate) of «هذا»; «أم» is the connected (muttaṣila) one, and the clause «أنتم لا تبصرون» is conjoined to the clause «سحر هذا».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «اصلوها» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and the clause «فاصبروا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «اصلوها». His words «سواء»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "your patience and its absence are equal"; the preposition «عليكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) (سواء). The clause «إنما تجزون» is resumptive, and «ما» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «فاكهين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun; the preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فاكهين». The clause «ووقاهم» is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «آتاهم»; «عذاب» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «كلوا» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of an implied saying; «هنيئا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). «بما»: the bāʾ governs the relative noun in the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «هنيئا».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «متكئين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {كُلُوا}; the preposition «على سرر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متكئين»; and the clause «وزوَّجْناهم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «وقاهم».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «والذين آمنوا..» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ}; the khabar (predicate) of «الذين» is «ألحقنا». The preposition «بإيمان» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اتَّبعتهم». The clause «وما ألتناهم» is conjoined to the clause «ألحقنا»; the preposition «من عملهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «من شيء»; «شيء» is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «كل امرئ رهين» is resumptive; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is genitive and attached to «رهين».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «وأمددناهم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {أَلْحَقْنَا}; the preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «لحم».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «يتنازعون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «أمددناهم», and the clause «لا لغو فيها» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «كأسا»; «لا» is negative, operating like «ليس».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «ويطوف» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {يَتَنَازَعُونَ}; the preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «غلمان»; and the clause «كأنهم لؤلؤ» is a naʿt of «غلمان».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «وأقبل» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يطوف», and the clause «يتساءلون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «أقبل».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «قالوا» is resumptive; the adverb (قبل) and the preposition (في أهلنا) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (كنا).

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «فمَنَّ الله» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying); «عذاب» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «إنا كنا» is resumptive; the preposition «من قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ندعوه». The clause «إنه هو البر» is resumptive; «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «إنه»; «الرحيم» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «فذكِّر» is resumptive, and the clause «فما أنت بكاهن» is resumptive. The preposition «بنعمة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «كاهن», the implied form being "you are neither a soothsayer nor mad, being clothed with a blessing"; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: «أم» is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), and the clause «يقولون» is resumptive; «شاعر» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied «هو»; the clause «نتربَّص» is a naʿt (adjective) of «شاعر»; «ريب» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «فإني معكم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «تربَّصوا»; «معكم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «المتربصين».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: (أم تأمرهم أحلامهم بهذا أم هم قوم طاغون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, as is the second «أم», and the clause after it is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: (أم يقولون تقوله بل لا يؤمنون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one and the clause is resumptive, as is the clause «لا يؤمنون».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The clause «فليأتوا» is resumptive, and the lām is the jussive lām of command; «مثله» is a naʿt (adjective). The clause «إن كانوا» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The clause «يستمعون» is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause «فليأتِ» is the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition, i.e. "if he claims that, let him bring".

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: «أجرا» is the second object; the preposition «من مغرم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مثقلون». The clause «فهم مثقلون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «تسألهم».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «فهم يكتبون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «عندهم الغيب».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: His words «فالذين كفروا»: a case of the overt noun occurring in the place of a pronoun, i.e. "then they are the ones outwitted"; so the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يريدون». «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «غير» is a naʿt (adjective); «ما» in «عمَّا» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied word that makes «سبحان» accusative; «سبحان» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the preposition «من السماء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ساقطا»; «سحاب» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied «هو».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «فذرهم» is resumptive; «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective); the preposition «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يصعقون».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from {يَوْمَهُمُ}; «شيئا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a little or a great sufficing"; and the clause «ولا هم ينصرون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «لا يغني».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: (وإن للذين ظلموا عذابا دون ذلك) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; the adverb «دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «عذابا»; the clause «ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «واصبر» is resumptive, as is the clause «فإنك بأعيننا»; the preposition «بحمد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «سَبِّح»; the adverb «حين» is attached to «سبِّح».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The wāw is conjunctive; the preposition «من الليل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فسبِّحه», and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); «إدبار» is a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the position of «من الليل», since its position is the accusative.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, يَوْم تمور السَّمَاء مورا: the governing word in يوم is واقع, i.e. "the punishment of your Lord will surely occur on the day the heaven sways" (إن عذاب ربك لواقع يوم تمور السماء). دافع does not govern it, because what is negated does not govern what comes before the negating particle: you do not say طعامَك ما زيد آكلا ("your food, Zayd is not eating"), whether you put آكلا in the nominative or the accusative or bring the بـ onto it. But if you put الطعام in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and make آكلا fall upon a هاء [referring to it], it is permissible, and what follows الطعام is its khabar (predicate); and omitting the هاء is ugly.
His saying فويل للمكذبين: a mubtadaʾ (subject) governing يومئذ, and للمكذبين is the khabar (predicate). The فاء is the answer to the preceding sentence, and that is good because the speech contains the sense of a condition, since the meaning is "when what was mentioned comes to pass, then woe that day to the deniers".

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying هَذِه النَّار: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), [the whole] spoken [by an implied saying]; its implied form is "it will be said to them: this is the Fire" (يقال لهم هذه النار). Like it in the implying of the saying is His saying كلوا واشربوا, i.e. "it will be said to them: eat and drink".

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying هَنِيئًا: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:29-29.t: His saying بكاهن وَلَا مَجْنُون: in ordinary speech the accusative is permissible by conjunction with the position of بكاهن in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, and the nominative is permissible by conjunction with the position of بكاهن in the dialect of Banū Tamīm, and by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "nor is he mad" (ولا هو مجنون).

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying سَحَاب مركوم: nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "this is a cloud" (هذا سحاب).
His saying يَوْم لَا يُغني: يوم is accusative as a badal (substitute) of يومهم, and يومهم is accusative by يلاقوا as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); its accusative is not as an adverb.

mekki-muskil:45-45.t: His saying فذرهم: its origin is فاوذرهم, but the wāw was omitted because it has the meaning of فدعهم, so it was treated like its counterpart in meaning and like what stands in its place, because they dispensed with the use of ودع by their saying ترك; likewise وذرهم was not used, just as ودع was not used. The wāw was omitted from يدع only because it is on the pattern of يزن, the دال being like the زاي in vowelling; but the دال in يدع was given a fatḥa because of the guttural letter after it, and its origin is the kasra, like the زاي of يزن. So the wāw was omitted according to the rule, because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra, and it was omitted from يذر because it has the meaning of يدع. The mention of this has preceded.

mekki-muskil:49-49.t: His saying وإدبار النُّجُوم: إدبار is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān); its implied form is "and glorify Him at the time of the stars' retreating" (وسبحه وقت إدبار النجوم). Like it is وإدبار السجود in the reading of whoever gives the hamza a kasra. As for whoever gives it a fatḥa in [Sūrat] Qāf, he made it the plural of دُبُر, which is an adverb used with latitude; it is related from the Arabs: جئتك دبر الصلاة ("I came to you after the prayer"). All of this is only by omission of "time" (وقت), just as you say جئتك مقدم الحاج وخفوق النجم ("I came to you at the arrival of the pilgrims and the setting of the star"), i.e. at the time of that.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿والطور﴾: the wāw is the wāw of oath; الطور is the thing sworn by, genitive (majrūr) by the wāw, and the sign of its genitive is the kasra; it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم (I swear); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وكتاب مسطور﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra; and مسطور is a naʿt (adjective), genitive with the kasra.
