muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿في رق منشور﴾: في رق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مسطور﴾, or another naʿt (adjective) of كتاب; and منشور is a naʿt of ﴿رق﴾, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿والبيت المعمور﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; البيت is conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra; and المعمور is a naʿt (adjective), genitive with the kasra.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿والسقف المرفوع﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; السقف is conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra; and المرفوع: a naʿt (adjective), genitive.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿والبحر المسجور﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; البحر is conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra; and المسجور is a naʿt (adjective), genitive with the kasra.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿إن عذاب ربك لواقع﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); عذاب is its noun; ربك is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the lām is the lām of the oath, a replacement for the shifted lām (al-muzaḥlaqa), giving emphasis; واقع is the khabar (predicate) of inna; and the clause is the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ما له من دافع﴾: ما is negating. وله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ومن: a redundant (ṣila) preposition. ودافع: genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). This clause is a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾, or a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿واقع﴾, i.e.: occurring, not to be repelled; or it is parenthetical between the adverb in His words ﴿يوم تمور السماء﴾ and what it is attached to, namely His words ﴿واقع﴾, and so it has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يوم تمور السماء مورا﴾: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿واقع﴾, i.e.: the punishment occurs on that day. The clause ﴿ما له من دافع﴾ is parenthetical between the adverb and what it is attached to. It has been said: the adverb is attached to ﴿دافع﴾. The clause ﴿تمور السماء﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; and مورًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) with the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وتسير الجبال سيرا﴾: the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿تمور السماء مورًا﴾; the wāw is conjunctive; تسير is an imperfect verb; الجبال is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); and سيرًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) with the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فويل يومئذ للمكذبين﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause), the implied form being: if what has been mentioned takes place, then woe to whoever denies Allah and His Messenger. ﴿ويل﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); it was permissible to begin with it because it carries the meaning of a supplication. ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم is an adverb (ẓarf) of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ويل﴾; and إذٍ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: so woe to them on the day when that occurs. وللمكذبين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ويل﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t: ﴿الذين هم في خوض يلعبون﴾: الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of المكذبين; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); وفي خوض: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يلعبون﴾; the clause يلعبون is the khabar (predicate) of هم; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا﴾: the adverb (ẓarf) is a badal (substitute) from ﴿يوم تمور السماء مورًا﴾ or from ﴿يومئذ﴾ before it; the clause يدعون is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; يدعون is an imperfect verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); وإلى نار جهنم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يدعون﴾; and دعًّا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿هذه النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون﴾: the clause is accusative by an omitted verb of saying, i.e.: that is said to them. هذه is a mubtadaʾ (subject); النار is the khabar (predicate); التي is a naʿt (adjective); the clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position. كان is an abrogating past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; وبها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبون﴾; and the clause تكذبون is the khabar of kāna.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿أفسحر هذا﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī), and the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to something omitted, its implied form being: you used to say of the revelation: this is sorcery; so is this sorcery? سحر is a fronted khabar (predicate), and هذا is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أم أنتم لا تبصرون﴾: أم: connected (muttaṣila); and it has been said: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza, the implied form being: بل أأنتم لا تبصرون؟ (rather, do you not see?). أنتم is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause لا تبصرون is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿اصلوها فاصبروا أو لا تصبروا سواء عليكم﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is conjunctive; اصبروا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; أو is a conjunction; لا is the prohibitive lā; تصبروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾; سواء is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: your patience and the abandonment of it are equal; وعليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سواء﴾; and it has been said: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e.: the two matters are equal for you.
﴿إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون﴾: إنما is the restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); تجزون is an imperfect verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ما is a relative noun, a second mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿كنتم تعملون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause تعملون is its khabar; and the clause ﴿إنما تجزون...﴾ gives the reason for the equality.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿إن المتقين في جنات ونعيم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); المتقين is its noun; وفي جنات is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; نعيم is conjoined to جنات; and the speech is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿فاكهين بما آتاهم ربهم ووقاهم ربهم عذاب الجحيم﴾: فاكهين: a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فاكهين﴾; and the clause ﴿آتاهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and it together with what it enters upon is construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿فاكهين﴾; and the clause ﴿آتاهم﴾ is the ṣila of the maṣdar-forming ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. ﴿آتاهم﴾ is a past verb, the hāʾ is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ﴿ربهم﴾ is a postponed fāʿil (agent). ﴿ووقاهم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and وقاهم: a past verb, the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the overt pronoun is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi. The clause ﴿وقاهم﴾ is conjoined to the ṣila clause, i.e.: rejoicing in their Lord's giving and in His protecting them from the punishment of Hellfire. Or the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with قد implied, according to those who require that a past verb serving as a ḥāl be accompanied by it.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿كلوا﴾: an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying) of an omitted verb of saying.
﴿واشربوا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿اشربوا﴾ is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿هنيئا﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e.: مُهَنَّأً (made wholesome); or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a naʿt (adjective) of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: أكلا هنيئا (a wholesome eating).
﴿بما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كلوا أو اشربوا﴾.
﴿كنتم﴾: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; the clause ﴿كنتم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿تعملون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿تعملون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of kāna.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿متكئين على سرر مصفوفة وزوجناهم بحور عين﴾: متكئين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun latent in His words ﴿في جنات﴾, i.e.: being in gardens in the state of reclining; or from the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿كلوا﴾, or from the object of ﴿آتاهم﴾, or from the object of ﴿وقاهم﴾; وعلى سرر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) متكئين; مصفوفة is a naʿt (adjective) of سرر; the wāw is a conjunction; زوجناهم is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وبحور is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿زوجناهم﴾; and عين is a naʿt of حور.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿والذين آمنوا واتبعتهم ذريتهم بإيمان ألحقنا بهم ذريتهم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is the clause ألحقنا بهم ذريتهم. It has been said: it is accusative by an omitted verb, the implied form being: وأكرمنا الذين آمنوا (and We honoured those who believed). It has also been said: ﴿الذين آمنوا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿حور عين﴾. The clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position. واتبعتهم ذريتهم is conjoined to ﴿آمنوا﴾; وبإيمان is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ذريتهم; the clause ألحقنا بهم ذريتهم is the khabar of الذين; and the clause ﴿والذين آمنوا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء كل امرئ بما كسب رهين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ألتناهم is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من عملهم is a ḥāl; من is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and شيء is genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is a second object; كل is a mubtadaʾ; امرئ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); بما: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ما is relative or maṣdar-forming; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رهين﴾; and رهين is the khabar of كل.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وأمددناهم بفاكهة ولحم مما يشتهون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; أمددناهم is conjoined to what preceded; وبفاكهة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أمددناهم﴾; لحم is conjoined to فاكهة; ومما is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause يشتهون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t: ﴿يتنازعون فيها كأسا لا لغو فيها ولا تأثيم﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and it has been said: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of أمددناهم. يتنازعون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); وفيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتنازعون﴾; كأسًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لا is the lā of generic negation, left inoperative because it is repeated; لغو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿فيها﴾; ولا تأثيم is conjoined to it; and what made it permissible to begin with it is that the negation precedes it.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t: ﴿ويطوف عليهم غلمان لهم كأنهم لؤلؤ مكنون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يطوف is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); وعليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يطو ف﴾ [Translator's note: so spaced in the source; read ﴿يطوف﴾]; غلمان is the fāʿil (agent) of يطوف; ولهم is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿غلمان﴾; كأن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; لؤلؤ is its khabar (predicate); مكنون is a naʿt of لؤلؤ; and the clause كأنهم is a second naʿt.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أقبل بعضهم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); وعلى بعض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أقبل; and the clause يتساءلون is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿قالوا إنا كنا قبل في أهلنا مشفقين﴾: قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause كنا is its khabar (predicate); the clause إنا كنا is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying); قبل is an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and مشفقين is the khabar of kāna.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿فمن الله علينا ووقانا عذاب السموم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; من الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); وعلينا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مَنَّ﴾; ووقانا is conjoined to مَنَّ; and عذاب السموم is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿إنا كنا من قبل ندعوه إنه هو البر الرحيم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ومن قبل is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause ندعوه is the khabar (predicate) of كنا; the clause كنا is the khabar of inna; إن is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); البر الرحيم are two khabars of إنه; and the clause إنه gives the reason (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿فذكر فما أنت بنعمت ربك بكاهن ولا مجنون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); ذكر is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: أنت (you); ﴿فما﴾: the fāʾ gives the reason for the command, and ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negating mā that operates like laysa; ﴿أنت﴾ is the noun of mā; ﴿بنعمة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the negated clause, and the bāʾ is causal, i.e.: you are not a soothsayer nor a madman because of your Lord's favour upon you. It has been said: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is ﴿بكاهن﴾ or ﴿مجنون﴾, and the bāʾ is for accompaniment (al-mulābasa), the implied form being: you are not a soothsayer nor a madman while being endowed with your Lord's favour; on this view it is a permanent ḥāl (ḥāl lāzima). It has also been said: the bāʾ is for the oath, and ﴿نعمة ربك﴾ is the thing sworn by, placed between the noun of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾ and its khabar (predicate), so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: أقسم (I swear), and the answer to the oath is omitted, i.e.: by your Lord's favour, you are not a soothsayer nor a madman. ﴿ربك﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the kāf is a pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بكاهن﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿كاهن﴾ is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in form; and the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿ولا مجنون﴾ are conjoined to ﴿كاهن﴾.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿أم يقولون شاعر نتربص به ريب المنون﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza, the implied form being: بل أيقولون شاعر؟ (rather, do they say: a poet?). ﴿يقولون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿شاعر﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿نتربص به﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of شاعر; وبه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نتربص﴾; and ﴿ريب المنون﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:31-31.t: ﴿قل تربصوا فإني معكم من المتربصين﴾: قل is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: أنت (you); تربصوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the fāʾ gives the reason for the command, which is intended as a threat; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun; معكم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ومن المتربصين is the khabar (predicate) of inna; and the clause تربصوا is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying).

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿أم تأمرهم أحلامهم بهذا﴾: أم is a conjunction meaning «بل» (rather); تأمرهم is an imperfect verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أحلامهم is the fāʿil (agent); and وبهذا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تأمرهم﴾.
﴿أم هم قوم طاغون﴾: أم is conjunctive; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and قوم the khabar (predicate); and طاغون is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:33-33.t: ﴿أم يقولون تقوله بل لا يؤمنون﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza, the implied form being: بل أيقولون تقوله؟ (rather, do they say: he has fabricated it?), and the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; or ﴿أم﴾ is connected (muttaṣila), in which case a clause must be implied so that the balance (al-taʿādul) is sound, the implied form being: do they acknowledge it, or do they say: he has fabricated it? The clause ﴿تقوّله﴾ is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying). ﴿يقولون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); تقوله is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: هو (he).

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿فليأتوا بحديث مثله﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause), and the lām is the lām of command; يأتوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); وبحديث is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يأتوا﴾; and مثله is a naʿt (adjective) of حديث.
﴿إن كانوا صادقين﴾: إن is conditional; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the wāw of the plural is its noun; صادقين is its khabar (predicate); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of in is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t: ﴿أم خلقوا من غير شيء﴾: conjoined to what preceded; ومن غير شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلقوا﴾; and أم هم الخالقون is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿أم خلقوا السماوات والأرض﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza; ﴿خلقوا﴾ is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); السماوات is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra; and الأرض is conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw, accusative with the fatḥa.
﴿بل لا يوقنون﴾: بل: a particle of transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); لا is negating; يوقنون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause ﴿لا يوقنون﴾ has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t: ﴿أم عندهم خزائن ربك﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza; the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); خزائن is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); هم is a mubtadaʾ, and المسيطرون is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿أم لهم سلم يستمعون فيه فليأت مستمعهم بسلطان مبين﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); سلم is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يستمعون is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سلم﴾; وفيه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يستمعون﴾; فليأت: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it is the answer of an implied condition, its implied form being: if they claim that, then let him bring; the lām is the lām of command; يأت is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; مستمعهم is the fāʿil (agent); وبسلطان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يأت; and مبين is a naʿt.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t: ﴿أم له البنات ولكم البنون﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿البنات﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿لكم البنون﴾ is conjoined to ﴿له البنات﴾.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿أم تسألهم أجرا فهم من مغرم مثقلون﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza; تسألهم is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) whose implied form is: أنت (you), and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أجرًا is a second mafʿūl bihi; the fāʾ is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ومن مغرم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مثقلون﴾; and مثقلون is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:41-41.t: ﴿أم عندهم الغيب فهم يكتبون﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza; the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); الغيب is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the fāʾ is conjunctive; هم is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause يكتبون is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿أم يريدون كيدا فالذين كفروا هم المكيدون﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza; يريدون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); كيدًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is conjunctive; الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, which has been pointed out before; the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; هم is a mubtadaʾ and المكيدون its khabar (predicate); and the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿أم لهم إله غير الله سبحان الله عما يشركون﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); إله is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); غير الله is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿إله﴾; سبحان is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿عما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿سبحان﴾; and the clause ﴿يشركون﴾ has no grammatical position, because ﴿ما﴾ is relative or maṣdar-forming.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t: ﴿وإن يروا كسفا من السماء ساقطا يقولوا سحاب مركوم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; يروا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), and the sign of its jussive is the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); كسفًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من السماء is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كسفًا﴾; ساقطا is a naʿt of ﴿كسفًا﴾; the apodosis clause has no grammatical position; يقولوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); سحاب is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); and مركوم is a naʿt of سحاب.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿فذرهم حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي فيه يصعقون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); ذرهم is an imperative verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); حتى is a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; يلاقوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by an implicit أن after حتى [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb is in fact accusative (manṣūb) by the implicit أن, the dropping of the nūn being the sign of the accusative]; the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb is genitive by حتى; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ذرهم; يومهم is a mafʿūl bihi; الذي is a naʿt (adjective) of يومهم; وفيه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to His words ﴿يصعقون﴾; and the clause يصعقون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي.

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿يوم لا يغني عنهم كيدهم شيئا ولا هم ينصرون﴾: يوم is a badal (substitute) from يومهم; the clause لا يغني is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb (ẓarf) to it; وعنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يغني﴾; كيدهم is the fāʿil (agent) of يغني; شيئًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negating; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause ينصرون is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وإن للذين ظلموا عذابا دون ذلك ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون﴾: the wāw is resumptive; إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); وللذين is its fronted khabar (predicate); the clause كفروا [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in this ayah is ظلموا] is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. عذابًا is the postponed noun of inna; دون is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذابًا﴾; ذلك is a demonstrative, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿وإن للذين...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ولكن: the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and لكن is an abrogating particle of rectification (al-istidrāk); أكثرهم is its noun; and the clause ﴿لا يعلمون﴾ is the khabar of lākin.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿واصبر لحكم ربك فإنك بأعيننا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; اصبر is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: أنت (you); ولحكم ربك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) اصبر; the fāʾ gives the reason (taʿlīliyya); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the kāf is its noun; and وبأعيننا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿وسبح بحمد ربك حين تقوم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; سبح is conjoined to واصبر; وبحمد ربك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. endowed with the praise of your Lord; حين is an adverb attached to ﴿سبح﴾; and the clause تقوم is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it.

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿ومن الليل فسبحه وإدبار النجوم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ومن الليل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سبحه﴾; سبحه is an imperative verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and إدبار النجوم is a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in for the adverb (ẓarf).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: Genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: A wāw of conjunction, not a wāw of oath. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda said: مَسْطُورٍ means "written". The grammarians permitted مصطور, changing the sīn into ṣād to bring it closer to the ṭāʾ.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
[فِي رَقٍّ مَنْشُورٍ] is part of the complement (ṣila) of مسطور, i.e. written on parchment. And the rajaz poet said:
438-
إنّي وأسطار سطرن سطرا
(Indeed I — by lines that were written line upon line…)

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: Conjoined, i.e. "inhabited" by those who enter it. One says: عمر المنزل (the dwelling was inhabited), so it is عامر; and عمرته (I inhabited it), so it is معمور. And if you want the transitive of "عمر المنزل" [in the sense of causing], you say أعمرته.

nahhas-irab:5-8.t: وَالسَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ (5) is conjoined, and likewise وَالْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ (6). The answer to the oath is إِنَّ عَذابَ رَبِّكَ لَواقِعٌ (7). Qatāda said: i.e. on the Day of Resurrection, i.e. it will befall the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: they will move. Abū Jaʿfar said: One says مار الشيء when a thing turns about; and the verse of al-Aʿshā is recited [in the basīṭ metre]: 439-
كأنّ مشيتها من بيت جارتها ... مور السّحابة لا ريث ولا عجل
(As though her walk from her neighbour's house were the drifting of a cloud, neither slow nor hasty.)
 And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: تمور means "it will split".

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَتَسِيرُ الْجِبالُ, i.e. from their places, سَيْراً.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: This fāʾ has entered because the speech contains the meaning of a conditional (mujāzāh). Similar to it is "فالكلم اسم وفعل وحرف جاء لمعنى" (so speech is noun, verb, and particle that has come for a meaning): the implied form is "when you have paid attention to it, then it is such-and-such". [In] the verse, the implied form is: "when this is so, then woe on that day to the deniers".

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: I.e. in temptation and confusion, يلعبون, i.e. heedless of what is intended for them. الَّذِينَ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of المكذبين.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: يوم is accusative as a badal (substitute) from يومئذ. Qābūs related from his father from Ibn ʿAbbās: يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلى نارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا — he said: they are shoved on their necks until they are driven to the Fire.

nahhas-irab:14-15.t: I.e. it is said to them; and this was omitted.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
اصْلَوْها, i.e. suffer its heat and its severity. فَاصْبِرُوا أَوْ لا, i.e. [be patient] over its pain and its severity.
تَصْبِرُوا. سَواءٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. patience and impatience are alike for you. عَلَيْكُمْ إِنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ, i.e. those who feared Allah, Majestic and Mighty, by avoiding disobedience to Him and performing His obligatory duties. فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ is in the position of the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

nahhas-irab:18-19.t: فَكِهِينَ is [accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The nominative is permissible outside the Qur'an, as the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». بِما آتاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ: by what He gave them and provided them with. وَوَقاهُمْ: its imperfect is weak in two respects, in its first radical and its last radical. Abū Jaʿfar said: As for its weakness in its first radical, its original form is يوقيه; the wāw was dropped because it is between a yāʾ and a kasra. Its weakness in its last radical is because it became vowelless in the position of the nominative, owing to the heaviness of the ḍamma on it. The implied form is: it is said to them: كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (19). هَنِيئاً is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and its meaning is: without any harm, grief or ill effect overtaking you in your eating or your drinking.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
مُتَّكِئِينَ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). عَلى سُرُرٍ مَصْفُوفَةٍ: [سرر] is the plural of سرير, and سرر [with a vowelless rāʾ] is permissible because of the heaviness of the ḍamma. مَصْفُوفَةٍ is a naʿt (adjective). وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ بِحُورٍ عِينٍ, i.e. We joined them with them. Abū ʿUbayda said: الحور is intense blackness of the eye and intense whiteness of the white of the eye. Abū Jaʿfar said:
الحور in the language is whiteness; from it is "al-khubz al-ḥuwwārī" (white bread). عِينٍ is the plural of عيناء, and it is on the pattern fuʿl; the ḍamma was replaced by a kasra because of its adjacency to the yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَالَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject). آمَنُوا is its ṣila (relative clause). وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ بِإِيمانٍ is included with it in the ṣila. أَلْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. This reading is transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and it has a connected chain of transmission (isnād) from the ḥadīth of al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī from al-Aʿmash from Ibrāhīm from ʿAlqama from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he corrected a man [reading] وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ بِإِيمانٍ أَلْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ with the singular in both places, some twenty times. This is the reading of the Kufans. Al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr read ذرياتهم in the plural in both places. The Medinans read وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ بِإِيمانٍ أَلْحَقْنا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ. [Translator's note: the Medinan reading is printed identically to the Kufan one; in the known accounts it is the singular in the first place and the plural ذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ in the second. Likewise Abū ʿAmr is usually reported with the plural only in the second place.] The meanings in this are close to one another, even though the heart inclines more to the singular, because of what is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and from Ibn ʿAbbās. Abū ʿUbayd argued for the singular from His saying, Majestic and Mighty: مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ آدَمَ [Maryam: 58], and there is nothing more numerous than the progeny of Ādam, upon him be peace. He said: and this is [a matter of] consensus, so the way to deal with what is disputed is to refer it back to it. وَما أَلَتْناهُمْ مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ: one says ألته يألته and لاته يليته when he diminishes it. «من» in عَمَلِهِمْ is partitive, and in مِنْ شَيْءٍ it is for emphasis. كُلُّ امْرِئٍ بِما كَسَبَ رَهِينٌ is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, i.e. every person is held in pledge for what he has done; no one is seized for another's sin.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ بِفاكِهَةٍ: they are these who have been mentioned. وَلَحْمٍ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ, i.e. that they desire it (يشتهونه); the hāʾ was omitted because of the length of the noun [i.e. the relative clause].

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: يَتَنازَعُونَ فِيها كَأْساً لا لَغْوٌ فِيها وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ (23): this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of the two cities [Basra and Kufa], except Abū ʿAmr; and it is related from al-Ḥasan لا لَغْوٌ فِيها وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ. [Translator's note: al-Ḥasan's variant is printed identically to the main reading; from what follows, the variant meant is presumably the accusative without nunation, لا لَغْوَ فِيها وَلا تَأْثِيمَ.] The nominative is from two angles: one of them is that «لا» is in the status of «ليس»; and the other is that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Abū ʿUbayd likened it to His saying, Majestic and Mighty: لا فِيها غَوْلٌ [al-Ṣāffāt: 47], and he chose the nominative. Abū Jaʿfar said: It does not resemble it according to any grammarian I know of, because when you separate [lā from its noun] nothing but the nominative is permitted, and so it is with لا فِيها غَوْلٌ; but when you do not separate, the nominative and the accusative without nunation are both permitted, and so it is with لا لَغْوٌ فِيها وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ. Had the two been one, as he said, it would not have been permitted. لا لَغْوٌ فِيها وَلا تَأْثِيمٌ: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read it so, and it is permissible and good according to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ. Its accusative is by way of absolute negation (al-tabriya) according to the Kufans; as for the Basrans, they made the two things one thing.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ غِلْمانٌ لَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ, i.e. in purity. مَكْنُونٌ: for that makes it purer and of a clearer whiteness.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Ibn Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: this is at the second blowing [of the Trumpet].

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: The khabar (predicate) of كان, i.e. before this; and «قبل» was made a ghāya (a word cut off from its annexed term) ...

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
Allah favoured them by forgiving the minor sins and by not taking them to account, through blessings that outweigh the deeds, as is related from the Prophet ﷺ: «No one will enter Paradise by his deeds.» It was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
«Not even I, unless Allah envelops me in mercy from Him.»

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: This is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza; Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ. [Translator's note: both readings are printed identically in the source; from the discussion, the second is أَنَّهُ with fatḥa.] Abū Jaʿfar [al-Naḥḥās] said: The kasra is clearer, because it is a statement of this, so it is more eloquent to begin [a new sentence]; the fatḥa is permissible, and its meaning is "we call upon Him because He is" or "since He is". Abū ʿUbayd opposed this reading, because he chose the kasra and because its meaning [with fatḥa] is "we call upon Him for this [reason]". This objection does not require forbidding the reading with fatḥa, because they call upon Him because He is thus, and this is permanent for Him, Majestic and Mighty, without interruption. Analogous to this is "لبّيك أنّ الحمد والنعمة لك" (At Your service; indeed praise and blessing are Yours), with fatḥa and kasra on إن. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْبَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ — he said: kind to His servants. Someone else said: merciful to His creatures, and He does not punish them after repentance.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
فَذَكِّرْ فَما أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِكاهِنٍ: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. you do not say what soothsayers say.
وَلا مَجْنُونٍ is conjoined to بكاهن; the accusative is permissible according to the position, in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; and the nominative is permissible in the dialect of Banū Tamīm, with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ شاعِرٌ: with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ: Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا, i.e. take your time and wait. فَإِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ, until the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, comes concerning you.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلامُهُمْ بِهذا: Ibn Zayd said: in the Jāhiliyya they used to be called "the people of understanding (ahl al-aḥlām)"; so the meaning is: or does their understanding command them to worship idols that are deaf and dumb? It was also said: أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلامُهُمْ to say to the one who came to them with the truth and proofs, forbidding wrong and commanding right: شاعِرٌ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that الأحلام here are the intellects and minds. أَمْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طاغُونَ, i.e. their understanding did not command them to do this; rather, they passed beyond faith to disbelief.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: I.e. they do not bring any proof that he invented it and fabricated it; rather, they do not believe. The Kufans say that «بل» only comes after a negation, so they construe the speech according to these meanings; and if they do not find that, they do not permit it to come after an affirmative.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: I.e. if they are truthful in [claiming] that he invented it, then they are the people of the tongue and the language, so let them bring a recitation like it.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ: there are several answers on it. Among the best of them: or were they created without a father or mother, so that they would be stones with no intellects by which to understand? It was said: the meaning is: or were they created without a Maker who made them, so they accept nothing from anyone? أَمْ هُمُ الْخالِقُونَ, i.e. are they the lords? For to the Lord belong command and prohibition.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: أَمْ خَلَقُوا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ, i.e. are they the ones who created the heavens and the earth, so that they would not acknowledge the One whom nothing resembles? بَلْ لا يُوقِنُونَ: it was said: the meaning is "they do not know and do not draw inferences"; and it was said: their conduct is the conduct of one who does not know. Among the best things said about it is that the meaning is: they have no certainty about the threat and the punishment Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has prepared for the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection; so they disbelieve and disobey because they have no certainty about the punishment of that [day].

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: أَمْ عِنْدَهُمْ خَزائِنُ رَبِّكَ, i.e. so that they could be self-sufficient by them. أَمْ هُمُ الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: المسيطرون are those given dominion. المسيطر in the speech of the Arabs is the tyrant, the domineering one, who is arrogant towards Allah, Majestic and Mighty. It is derived from السطر (line), as though he is the one who draws a line upon people, preventing them from what they want. Its basic form is with sīn, and changing the sīn into ṣād is permissible because a ṭāʾ comes after it; and on this [basis] is the main body of writing (al-sawād) in this word.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ (38). أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ, i.e. on which they listen to revelation from heaven, and so claim that what they follow has been revealed? فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ, i.e. with a clear proof, as the Prophet ﷺ brought it.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: As you say; and that is an unjust division.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: مَغْرَمٍ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. or do you ask them for wealth, so that they are مثقلون (weighed down) at having to pay anything, i.e. that weighs heavily on them?

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: أَمْ عِنْدَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ, i.e. they do not know the unseen; so how can they say "We will not believe in a messenger who eats food and walks in the markets", and say "A poet: we await for him the accident of fate"? فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ, i.e. so they write for people whatever they wish of the unseen and inform them of it?

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: أَمْ يُرِيدُونَ كَيْداً, i.e. a scheme to humiliate the Prophet ﷺ and destroy him, and against the believers. فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هُمُ الْمَكِيدُونَ, i.e. they are the ones humiliated and destroyed, coming to the punishment of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. [Translator's note: «الصابرون» as printed; probably a misprint for «الصائرون» "coming to", which is how it is rendered here.]

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: أَمْ لَهُمْ إِلهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ, i.e. an object of worship that deserves worship. سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ, i.e. declaring Allah, Majestic and Mighty, free of what they worship besides Him.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كِسْفاً مِنَ السَّماءِ ساقِطاً: [كسف] is the plural of كسفة, like سدرة and سدر. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: كسفا — he said: He is saying "pieces". يَقُولُوا سَحابٌ مَرْكُومٌ: with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. they will say: "This piece is heaped-up cloud."

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
فَذَرْهُمْ: from يذر; the wāw was dropped from it, though it is only dropped from yafʿilu because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra, or from yafʿalu when it contains one of the guttural letters, and there is nothing of this in «يذر» that requires the dropping of the wāw. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: the wāw was dropped from it because it is in the sense of يدع, so it was made to follow it.
حَتَّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ: al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim read يُصْعَقُونَ; al-Ḥasan said: i.e. they are made to die. Al-Farrāʾ related from ʿĀṣim يُصْعَقُونَ, and this is not known from him. He said: one says صعق يصعق, and it is a well-known dialect form, just as all read فَصَعِقَ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ [al-Zumar: 68], and they did not read فصعق. And one says صعق يصعق, and أصعق is the transitive of صعق. [Translator's note: the variant forms in this passage are printed without distinguishing vowels; the readings discussed are يُصْعَقُونَ (passive, al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim) and يَصْعَقُونَ (active), and the forms صَعِقَ/صُعِقَ.]

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: يَوْمَ لا يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئاً is a badal (substitute) from the first يوم. وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ, i.e. no one will take retribution for them from those who punished them, nor protect them.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا عَذاباً دُونَ ذلِكَ: the most eminent in chain of transmission of what has been said about it is what Abū Isḥāq related from al-Barāʾ: وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا عَذاباً دُونَ ذلِكَ — he said: the punishment of the grave. Ibn Zayd said: the calamities in this world. The meaning of دُونَ ذلِكَ is "before the day on which they will be thunderstruck", which is the Day of Resurrection. وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ, i.e. they do not know that they will taste that punishment; and it was said: their conduct is the conduct of one who does not know.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: وَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ, i.e. for His judgement which He has decreed for you, and carry out His command and His prohibition and convey His message. فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنا, i.e. We see you and see your actions, and We surround you and protect you. عين has been given the plural أعين, though it is like بيت, and one does not say أبيت because of the heaviness of the ḍamma on the yāʾ; but this came with عين because it is feminine, and afʿul is common in the plural of feminines: they said شمال, أشمل and عناق, أعنق. أعيان has also been said, like أبيات. وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ: there are several views on its meaning. The view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk is that its meaning is "when you stand for prayer", after the opening takbīr (takbīrat al-iḥrām), saying: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise; blessed is Your name and exalted is Your majesty." It was said: the glorification (التسبيح) here is the opening takbīr, without which the prayer is not complete, because the meaning of تسبيح in the language is declaring Allah, Majestic and Mighty, free of every evil the polytheists ascribed to Him, and magnifying Him; and whoever says "Allāhu akbar" has done this. A third view is that the meaning is "when you rise from your sleep", and that this is on the day of the siesta, meaning the Ẓuhr prayer, because what is well known of people rising from their sleep for prayer is only for the Fajr prayer, and the Ẓuhr prayer and the Fajr prayer are mentioned after this. As for al-Ḍaḥḥāk's view that it concerns the opening of the prayer, it is far-fetched given the consensus of proof, because the opening [supplication] in prayer is not obligatory, and had Allah, Majestic and Mighty, commanded it, it would be obligatory — unless proof is established that it is by way of recommendation and guidance.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ: Ibn Zayd said: the ʿIshāʾ prayer. Someone else said: the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers. وَإِدْبارَ النُّجُومِ: there are two views on it. One of them is that it is for the two rakʿas of Fajr. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Zayd said: the Ṣubḥ prayer. He said: and this is more fitting, because it is an obligation from Allah the Exalted. وَإِدْبارَ النُّجُومِ is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "and glorify Him at the time of the setting of the stars", as [in] "I will come to you at the arrival of the pilgrims" (مقدم الحاجّ); but "I will come to you at the arrival of Zayd" is not permissible; this is only permitted in what is well known. This is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh.

safi-cedvel:11-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (ويل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) «[Note: An indefinite noun denoting censure, which made it valid to begin with it.]» , (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb) «[Note: Or indeclinable (mabnī) in the position of accusative, because it is annexed to a non-declinable word, namely إذ.]» , muḍāf to another adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ويل), and the tanwīn in it is a substitute for an omitted clause, i.e. the day when the punishment occurs; (للمكذّبين) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (ويل).
The clause «ويل ... للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if the matter of the punishment is thus, then woe to the deniers.
The clause «هم في خوض ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين), and the clause «يلعبون» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم) «[Note: Or it has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).]» 13- (يوم) an adverb, accusative, a badal (substitute) for يومئذ; (إلى نار) attached to (يدّعون), (دعّا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative..
The clause «يدّعون ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. 14- (هذه) a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar being (النار) «[Note: Or its khabar is the relative noun, and (النار) is a badal of the demonstrative.]» , (التي) a relative noun in the position of nominative, a naʿt (adjective) of النار; (بها) attached to (تكذّبون) ...
The clause «هذه النار» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied verb of saying «[Note: I.e. the keepers of Hell say to them: This is the Fire.]» , and the clause «كنتم بها تكذّبون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (التي), and the clause «تكذّبون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم. 15- (الهمزة) for the rebuking interrogative; (الفاء) conjunction; (سحر) a fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ (هذا), (أم) a particle that is the counterpart (muʿādil) of the interrogative hamza «[Note: The author of al-Kashshāf made it the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning (بل).]» , (لا) negative..
The clause «سحر هذا» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the reported speech, and the clause «أنتم لا تبصرون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause سحر هذا, and the clause «لا تبصرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم). 16- (أو) a conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing; (سواء) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "your patience" (صبركم) «[Note: al-Zamakhsharī made it a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar implied as "patience and impatience".]» , (عليكم) attached to (سواء), (إنّما) the restraining (kāffa) particle and the restrained (makfūfa) one, and (الواو) in (تجزون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: Or a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause after it is the ṣila of the relative noun.]» ...
The clause «اصلوها ... » has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the saying; the clause «اصبروا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اصلوها; the clause «لا تصبروا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اصبروا; the clause « (صبركم..) سواء» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical; the clause «تجزون..» has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation (taʿlīl) for the choice between patience and its absence; the clause «كنتم تعملون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما), and the interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ... ) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the recompense of what you used to ...
The clause «تعملون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(13) دعّا: a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral verb دعّ يدعّ, of the pattern (bāb) نصر, meaning he pushed him violently in his chest; its wazn is فعْل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي خَوْضٍ يَلْعَبُونَ» .
The original meaning of al-khawḍ is walking in water; it was then used figuratively for embarking upon anything, and it came predominantly to mean plunging into falsehood. Lying and rushing into falsehood are likened to a deep water which the player wades into. One says: خاض الفرات, i.e. he plunged into it; and خاض في الحديث, he went at length into the talk.
And one says: إنه يخوض المنايا, i.e. he throws himself into perils.

* Benefits:
The meanings of the hamza ...
The basic function of the hamza is to be a particle of interrogation, as in our saying: (أأنت فعلت هذا؟) "Did you do this?" But it may depart from genuine interrogation and occur with eight meanings:
1- Equalization (al-taswiya): One might imagine that what is meant by it is the hamza occurring after the word سواء, but that is not so; rather, just as it occurs after it, it occurs after:
(ما أبالي) and (ما أدري) and (ليت شعري) and the like. The rule is that it is the hamza that enters a clause in whose place a maṣdar may validly stand.
As in His saying, the Exalted: سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ, and like (ما أبالي أقمت أم قعدت) "I do not care whether you stood or sat"; the interpretation being (سواء عليهم الاستغفار وعدمه) and (ما أبالي بقيامك أو قعودك).
2- Invalidating denial (al-inkār al-ibṭālī): This requires that what follows it has not happened and that the one who claims it is a liar, as in His saying, the Exalted, in the verse we are dealing with: أَفَسِحْرٌ هذا أَمْ أَنْتُمْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ, and أَفَأَصْفاكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِالْبَنِينَ وَاتَّخَذَ مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ إِناثاً. And because this hamza conveys the negation of what follows it, it entails its affirmation if it is negated, since the negation of a negation is an affirmation; of this is His saying, the Exalted: أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكافٍ عَبْدَهُ and أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ. And of it is the saying of Jarīr about ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān:
ألستم خير من ركب المطايا ... وأندى العالمين بطون راح
(Are you not the best of those who ride mounts, and the most generous of all the worlds in the palms of their hands?)
It has been said: it is the most laudatory verse the Arabs ever composed; and if it were a genuine question, it would not be praise at all.
3- Rebuking denial (al-inkār al-tawbīkhī): It requires that what follows it has happened and that its doer is blameworthy, as in His saying, the Exalted: أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ, أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ, أَإِفْكاً آلِهَةً دُونَ اللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ.
4- Eliciting affirmation (al-taqrīr): Its meaning is your leading the addressee to acknowledge and confess a matter whose affirmation or negation is settled with him. The thing about which you elicit his acknowledgment must come directly after it. You say, in eliciting acknowledgment of the verb: أضربت زيدا؟; of the agent: أأنت ضربت زيدا؟; and of the object: أزيدا ضربت؟ — just as that is required with the thing asked about. And His saying, the Exalted: أَأَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ هذا؟ may be intended as a genuine question, in that they did not know he was the doer, or as eliciting affirmation.
5- Mockery (al-tahakkum), as in His saying, the Exalted: أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا.
6- Command (al-amr): as in His saying, the Exalted: أَأَقْرَرْتُمْ؟ i.e. acknowledge.
7- Wonder (al-taʿajjub): as in His saying, the Exalted: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ.
8- Finding something slow in coming (al-istibṭāʾ): as in His saying, the Exalted: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَما نَزَلَ مِنَ الْحَقِ

safi-cedvel:17-28.t:
* I'rab:
(في جنّات) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of inna; (فاكهين) ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of settledness (ḍamīr al-istiqrār) in the khabar of inna; (بما) attached to (فاكهين), the returning pronoun being omitted. The clause «إنّ المتقين في جنّات ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «آتاهم ربّهم ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما); and the clause «وقاهم ربّهم» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the khabar of inna «[Note: It may be a ḥāl, with قد implied ... or it is resumptive with no grammatical position.]» 19- (هنيئا) ḥāl, accusative (manṣūba), from the fāʿil (agent) of كلوا and اشربوا; (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.]» ...
The clause «كلوا ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied verb of saying «[Note: I.e. the angels say to them: Eat ...]» ; the clause «اشربوا ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause كلوا; the clause «كنتم تعملون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما), and the interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ... ) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (هنيئا); and the clause «تعملون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم. 20- (متّكئين) ḥāl, accusative, from the fāʿil of كلوا or اشربوا «[Note: Or from the latent pronoun in the khabar of inna.]» , (على سرر) attached to (متّكئين); (بحور) attached to (زوّجناهم); and the clause «زوّجناهم ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause وقاهم..
21- (الواو) conjunction; (الذين) a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) «[Note: al-Zamakhsharī conjoined it to (حور ... ), i.e. We paired them with wide-eyed houris and with believing companions.]» , (بإيمان) attached to (اتّبعتهم) «[Note: Or attached to (ألحقنا), the bāʾ being causal.]» , (بهم) attached to (ألحقنا), (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negative; (من عملهم) attached to (ألتناهم), (شيء) genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.]» ...
The clause «الذين آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّ المتّقين في جنّات; the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «اتّبعتهم ذرّيّتهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمنوا «[Note: The clause may be parenthetical between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar.]» ; the clause «ألحقنا بهم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين); the clause «ما ألتناهم ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause ألحقنا..
The clause «كلّ امرئ ... رهين» has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation (taʿlīl); the clause «كسب ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما), and the interpreted maṣdar (ما كسب ... ) is in the position of genitive by the causal bāʾ, attached to (رهين).
22- (الواو) conjunction; (بفاكهة) attached to (أمددناهم), (ممّا) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (لحم), the returning pronoun being omitted. The clause «أمددناهم ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause ألحقنا..
The clause «يشتهون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما). 23- (فيها) attached to (يتنازعون) «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يتنازعون.]» , (لا) negative, inoperative «[Note: Or operating like ليس, with (لغو) as the noun of لا.]» , (لغو) mubtadaʾ, nominative; (فيها) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), obligatory; (تأثيم) conjoined to لغو, nominative.
The clause «يتنازعون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive «[Note: Or it is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the relative noun الذين آمنوا ... and it may be a ḥāl from the object of أمددناهم.]» ; and the clause «لا لغو فيها..» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (كأسا). 24- (الواو) conjunction; (عليهم) attached to (يطوف), (لهم) a naʿt of غلمان ...
The clause «يطوف عليهم غلمان» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يتنازعون; the clause «كأنّهم لؤلؤ ... » is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of غلمان «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from غلمان, since it is qualified by the preposition and its genitive noun.]» 25- 26- (الواو) conjunction; (على بعض) attached to (أقبل), (قبل) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (مشفقين); (في أهلنا) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in مشفقين ...
The clause «أقبل بعضهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يطوف; the clause «يتساءلون ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of أقبل; the clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī); the clause «إنّا كنّا ... » is in the position of accusative as the reported speech; and the clause «كنّا ... مشفقين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna. 27- 28- (الفاء) conjunction, and likewise the wāw; (علينا) attached to (منّ), (قبل) like the first one «[Note: In verse (26) of this sūra.]» , in the position of genitive, attached to (ندعوه) ...
The clause «منّ اللَّه ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the reported speech; the clause «وقانا ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause منّ; the clause «انّا كنّا ... » has no grammatical position, being causal; the clause «كنّا ... ندعوه» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna; the clause «ندعوه ... » is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنّا; the clause «إنّه هو البرّ ... » has no grammatical position, being causal; and the clause «هو البرّ ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna (the second).

* Morphology:
(20) مصفوفة: feminine of مصفوف, a passive participle from the triliteral صفّ; its wazn is مفعول. (21) رهين: a derived adjective from the triliteral رهن, meaning مرهون (pledged); its wazn is فعيل. (23) تأثيم: a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral أثّم; its wazn is تفعيل..
(28) البرّ: the beneficent; an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral برّ, of the patterns (bāb) نصر, ضرب and فتح; its wazn is فعْل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The loose simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in His saying, the Exalted, «كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ مَكْنُونٌ» .
The youths are likened to pearls guarded in the shell, for their whiteness and purity, or to stored pearls, since only what is precious and of high value is stored; the point of similarity is whiteness and purity.

* Benefits:
The clause in the position of accusative as a ḥāl..
It occurs after a definite noun, because clauses after definite nouns are ḥāls and after indefinite nouns are adjectives; it likewise sometimes occurs after the wāw of the ḥāl, and it is always in the position of accusative. That is as in His saying, the Exalted: وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ. And of its occurrence after the wāw of the ḥāl is His saying, the Exalted: لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكارى, and his saying, upon him be blessing and peace: (أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد) "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating." And among the ḥāl clauses is His saying, the Exalted: ما يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ; the clause استمعوه is a ḥāl from the object of يأتيهم, or from its agent, and the clause (وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ) is a ḥāl from the agent of (استمعوه). And of it is His saying, the Exalted: أَوْ جاؤُكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ; the clause حصرت is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, and the grammarians imply an omitted (قد), i.e. (أو جاؤوكم قد حصرت صدورهم).

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, and the second one is causal; (ما) negative, operating like ليس; (بنعمة) genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in كاهن — or مجنون — «[Note: I.e. you are not a soothsayer, while being clothed in the grace of your Lord ... It may also be attached to the content of the negation — the intent of the verse — i.e. soothsaying and madness are negated from you because of Allah's grace upon you.]» , (كاهن) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation ...
The clause «ذكّر ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if the disbelievers describe you with soothsaying and madness, then remind them of Allah ... i.e. continue reminding them; and the clause «ما أنت ... بكاهن» has no grammatical position, being causal.

* Morphology:
(كاهن), an active participle from the triliteral (كهن), of the pattern (bāb) كرم; its wazn is فاعل, meaning one who tells of hidden matters without revelation.

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل plus the hamza, and it is for the rebuking interrogative «[Note: (أم) will be mentioned in the sūra fifteen times, all of them of the type of interrogative indicating rebuke and condemnation; it means بل once and بل plus the hamza another time.]» , (شاعر) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هو; (به) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نتربّص). The clause «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause « (هو) شاعر ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl); and the clause «نتربّص ... » is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of شاعر.

* Morphology:
(المنون), a noun for death. al-Zamakhsharī said: it is originally فعول from منّه, when he cut it, because death cuts off lifespans.

* Rhetoric:
The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying, the Exalted: نَتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ.
Here al-rayb is applied to events (calamities), al-rayb being doubt; events are likened to rayb, i.e. doubt, because they do not last and do not remain in one state.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (معكم) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) المتربصين; (من المتربّصين) the khabar (predicate) of inna. The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «تربصوا ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl); and the clause «إنّي ... من المتربّصين ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you wait, then I am with you.

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(أم تأمرهم) like أم يقولون «1» , (بهذا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تأمرهم), (أم) like the first one. The clause «تأمرهم أحلامهم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «هم قوم ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(أحلام), plural of حلم, a noun meaning intellect; its wazn is فعْل, with kasra then sukūn, and the wazn of أحلام is أفعال.

* Rhetoric:
The figurative usage (al-majāz): in His saying, the Exalted, أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلامُهُمْ بِهذا.
The commanding of their minds to that is a figure for leading to it, by the relation of causality. It is also possible that the minds were made commanders by way of implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): the minds are likened to an obeyed ruler, a likening concealed in the mind, and command is affirmed of them by way of imaginative attribution (takhyīl).

safi-cedvel:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(أم يقولون) its i'rab has passed «2» , and the pronoun in (تقوّله) refers back to the Noble Qur'an; (بل) for digression (iḍrāb); (لا) negative. The clause «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «تقوّله ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl); and the clause «لا يؤمنون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. 34- (الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (اللام) the lām of command; (بحديث) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتوا), (مثله) a naʿt (adjective) of حديث; (كانوا) an incomplete past verb, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ)..
The clause «يأتوا ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if they are truthful in their saying "he fabricated it", then let them bring ...
The clause «كانوا صادقين» has no grammatical position, being an explication of the implied condition ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(أم خلقوا) like أم يقولون «1» , and (الواو) in (خلقوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (من غير) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلقوا), (أم) like the first one. The clause «خلقوا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «هم الخالقون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(أم خلقوا) like أم يقولون «2» , (بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (لا) negative ...
The clause «خلقوا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «لا يوقنون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(عندهم) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (خزائن)..
The clause «عندهم خزائن ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «هم المصيطرون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(المصيطرون), plural of المصيطر, an active participle from the quadriliteral سيطر; its wazn is مفيعل. Four words share this wazn with it: المهيمن, المبيقر, المبيطر and المجيمر; the first three are active participles and the fourth is the name of a mountain. It is written in the Muṣḥaf with ṣād, the sīn having been changed to ṣād because it comes before ṭāʾ, like الصراط whose origin is السراط. al-Musayṭir is the subduer, the overpowering one, or the domineering tyrant.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(أم لهم سلّم) like أم عندهم خزائن «[Note: In verse (37) of the sūra.]» , (فيه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يستمعون), and the object of the verb is omitted, i.e. they listen to the speech of the angels on it «[Note: Or the verb is made to include the meaning of "they ascend".. and it may be attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of يستمعون, i.e. ascending on it.]» , (الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (اللام) the lām of command; (بسلطان) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil. The clause «لهم سلّم ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «يستمعون ... » is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of سلّم; and the clause «يأت مستمعهم» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if the listener claims that, then let him bring ...

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
Like أم عندهم خزائن «[Note: In verse (37) of this sūra.]» . The clause «له البنات ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «لكم البنون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one.

* Benefits:
- أم ...
Most often it is a conjunction conveying equivalence (al-muʿādala), as in our saying (أزيد في الدار أم عمرو) "Is Zayd in the house or ʿAmr?" and the saying of Zuhayr:
وما أدري ولست إخال أدري ... أقوم آل حصن أم نساء
(I do not know — and I do not think I shall know — whether the family of Ḥiṣn are men or women.)
It comes in several ways, among them:
That it be disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), which is of three kinds:
1- Preceded by a pure statement, as in His saying, the Exalted: تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ.
2- Preceded by a hamza not for interrogation, as in His saying, the Exalted: أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِها أَمْ لَهُمْ أَيْدٍ يَبْطِشُونَ بِها, since the hamza there is for denial, so it is equivalent to negation, and the connected (muttaṣila) أم does not occur after it.
3- Preceded by an interrogative other than the hamza, as in His saying, the Exalted: هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُماتُ وَالنُّورُ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ. al-Farrāʾ said: they say هل لك قبلنا حق أم أنت رجل ظالم "Do you have a right against us, or are you an unjust man?", meaning: rather, you are.
Likewise His saying, the Exalted, in the verse we are dealing with: أَمْ لَهُ الْبَناتُ وَلَكُمُ الْبَنُونَ, its implied form being: بل أله البنات ولكم البنون.
And the meaning of the disconnected أم: digression (iḍrāb) never leaves it, as has passed in the preceding examples.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(أم تسألهم) like أم يقولون «[Note: In verse (30) of this sūra.]» , (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause; (من مغرم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مثقلون). The clause «تسألهم ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «فهم ... مثقلون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تسألهم.

* Morphology:
(مثقلون), plural of مثقل ... a passive participle from the quadriliteral أثقل; its wazn is مفعَل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(أم عندهم الغيب) like أم عندهم خزائن «[Note: In verse (37) of the sūra.]» , (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause. The clause «عندهم الغيب ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «هم يكتبون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause عندهم الغيب; and the clause «يكتبون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(أم يريدون) like أم يقولون «[Note: In verse (30) of the sūra.]» , (الفاء) resumptive; (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl)» , (المكيدون) the khabar (predicate) of the relative noun. The clause «يريدون..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).

* Morphology:
(المكيدون), plural of المكيد, a passive participle from the triliteral كاد يكيد, on the wazn of مبيع. It contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by deletion; its origin is مكيود: the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the kāf before it; then the wāw was deleted because it is augmentative, then what precedes the yāʾ was given kasra for harmony, and it became مكيد.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(أم لهم إله) like أم عندهم خزائن «[Note: In verse (37) of the sūra.]» , (غير) a naʿt (adjective) of إله; (سبحان) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; (عمّا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) verb ... and the returning pronoun is omitted.
The clause «لهم إله ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause « (نسبّح) سبحان ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من السماء) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ساقطا), (سحاب) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هذا. The clause «يروا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «يقولوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) not joined with the fāʾ; and the clause « (هذا) سحاب ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(ساقطا), an active participle from the triliteral سقط; its wazn is فاعل. (مركوم), a passive participle from the triliteral ركم; its wazn is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:45-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (حتّى) a particle of limit and of the genitive; (يلاقوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after حتّى; (الذي) a relative noun in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of يومهم, and (الواو) in (يصعقون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), the returning pronoun being omitted.
The clause «ذرهم ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if they reach this limit of disbelief, then leave them ...
The clause «يلاقوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يلاقوا ... ) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ذرهم); and the clause «يصعقون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي). 46- (يوم) a badal (substitute) for يومهم, accusative; (لا) negative; (عنهم) attached to (يغني), (شيئا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. anything of availing.]» , (الواو) conjunction; (ينصرون) like يصعقون; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation ...
The clause «لا يغني عنهم كيدهم ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause «هم ينصرون» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause لا يغني ...
And the clause «ينصرون» is in the position of nominative of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم) «[Translator's note: the text reads «في محلّ رفع المبتدأ (هم)»; the word خبر (khabar, predicate) appears to have dropped out, i.e. "in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم)".]»

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (للذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of inna; (عذابا) the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (دون) an adverb, accusative, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (عذابا) «[Note: I.e. before that, or other than that.]» , (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative ...
The clause «إنّ للذين ظلموا عذابا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين); the clause «لكنّ أكثرهم لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one; and the clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of lākinna.

safi-cedvel:48-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لحكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اصبر), (الفاء) causal; (بأعيننا) attached to the khabar (predicate) of inna; (الواو) conjunction; (بحمد) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of سبّح, i.e. clothed in the praise of your Lord; (حين) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (سبّح).
The clause «اصبر ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «إنّك بأعيننا ... » has no grammatical position, being causal; and the clause «سبّح ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اصبر.
The clause «تقوم ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. 49- (الواو) conjunction; (من الليل) attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being قم — or سبّحه — (الفاء) conjunction — or redundant (zāʾida) — (الواو) conjunction; (إدبار) conjoined to حين, accusative «[Note: Or conjoined to the position of (من الليل), since its position is accusative by its being an adverbial ... or it is an adverb attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being سبّحه إدبار النجوم.. and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.]» ...
The clause « (قم) من الليل ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سبّح.
The clause «سبّحه (the one mentioned) » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (قم) «[Note: Or it has no grammatical position, being explicative, with the fāʾ redundant.]» .

* Morphology:
(إدبار), a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb أدبر; its wazn is إفعال ...
from the past tense, with kasra on its first letter and the addition of an alif before the last.

safi-cedvel:1-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is the wāw of the oath. (الطور) is the thing sworn by, genitive by the wāw, attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is أقسم. (الواو) is a conjunction in the five places. (في رقّ) is attached to an adjective of (كتاب) [Note: or attached to مسطور]. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, a substitute for the shifted lām. (ما) is negative. (له) is attached to a fronted khabar. (دافع) is genitive in form and nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ. (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (دافع) or to (واقع). (مورا) is an accusative absolute object, and likewise (سيرا).
Clause: « (أقسم) بالطور ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause. And the clause: «إنّ عذاب ربّك لواقع ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
